children.text: karabadarasadṛśam alikhaṃ bhuvanatalaṃ yatprasādataḥ kavayaḥ /
children.translated_text: By whose grace poets of subtle intellect

children.text: paśyanti sūkṣmamatayaḥ sā jayati sarasvatī devī || 1 ||
children.translated_text: perceive the surface of the world as [small as] a <s>karabadara</s> (jujube fruit in the hand) — that goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s> is victorious! || 1 ||

children.text: khinno 'si muñca śailaṃ bibhṛmo vayam iti vadatsu śithilabhujaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'You are weary — release the mountain! We shall bear it' — while the cowherds with arms drooping,

children.text: bharabhugnavitatabāhuṣu gopeṣu hasan harir jayati || 2 ||
children.translated_text: their arms bent under the burden, spoke thus, <s>Hari</s>, laughing, is victorious! || 2 ||

children.text: kaṭhinataradāmaveṣṭanalekhāsandehadāyino yasya /
children.translated_text: He whose belly-folds shine, causing doubt whether they are the marks

children.text: rājanti valivibhaṅgāḥ sa pātu dāmodaro bhavataḥ || 3 ||
children.translated_text: of the exceedingly hard rope-binding — may that <s>Dāmodara</s> protect you! || 3 ||

children.text: sa jayati himakaralekhā cakāsti yasyotsukomayā nihitā /
children.translated_text: Victorious is that crescent moon which gleams, placed upon [his head] with eagerness,

children.text: nayanapratīpakajjalajighṛkṣayā śirasi rajataśuktir iva || 4 ||
children.translated_text: as if it were a silver oyster-shell, out of desire to grasp the collyrium hostile to the eyes, placed on [<s>Śiva's</s>] head. || 4 ||

children.text: bhavati subhagatvam adhikaṃ vistāritaparaguṇasya sujanasya /
children.translated_text: The good fortune of a virtuous person who displays the merits of others greatly increases;

children.text: vahati vikāsitakumudo dviguṇaruciṃ himakarodyotaḥ || 5 ||
children.translated_text: the splendor of the moon, which causes the lotuses to bloom, bears a doubled radiance. || 5 ||

children.text: viṣadharato 'py ativiṣamaḥ khala iti na mṛṣā vadanti vidvāṃsaḥ /
children.translated_text: The wise do not speak falsely when they say that the wicked person, even more dangerous than a venomous serpent, is truly <s>ativiṣama</s> (exceedingly crooked);

children.text: yad ayaṃ nakuladveṣī sa kuladveṣī punaḥ piśunaḥ || 6 ||
children.translated_text: for this one is hostile to the mongoose-folk (<s>nakula-dveṣī</s>) and again a slanderer hostile to good families (<s>kula-dveṣī</s>). || 6 ||

children.text: atimaline kartavye bhavati khalānām atīva nipuṇā dhīḥ /
children.translated_text: In doing what is exceedingly foul, the intellect of the wicked becomes supremely skilled;

children.text: timire hi kauśikānāṃ rūpaṃ pratipadyate dṛṣṭiḥ || 7 ||
children.translated_text: indeed, in darkness the sight of owls assumes its [true] form. || 7 ||

children.text: hasta iva bhūtimalino laṅghayati yathā yathā khalaḥ sujanam /
children.translated_text: Just as a hand soiled with impurity [touching] a mirror,

children.text: darpaṇam iva taṃ kurute tathā tathā nirmalacchāyam || 8 ||
children.translated_text: the more the wicked person assails a good person, the more he renders him, like that mirror, of spotless reflection. || 8 ||

children.text: vidhvastaparaguṇānāṃ bhavati khalānām atīva malinatvam /
children.translated_text: The impurity of the wicked who have destroyed the virtues of others becomes extreme;

children.text: antaritaśaśirucām api salilamucāṃ malinim ābhyadhikaḥ || 9 ||
children.translated_text: even clouds that have obscured the moon's radiance become exceedingly dark. || 9 ||

children.text: sā rasavattā nihatā navakā vilasanti carati no kaṅkaḥ /
children.translated_text: That sense of <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic delight) has been laid low; new [pretenders] shine forth; the heron struts about;

children.text: sarasīva kīrtiśeṣaṃ gatavati bhuvi vikramāditye || 10 ||
children.translated_text: like a pond [drying up], when <s>Vikramāditya</s> has departed from the earth, only the fame remains. || 10 ||

children.text: aviditaguṇāpi satkavibhaṇitiḥ karṇeṣu vamati madhudhārām /
children.translated_text: Even without grasping its qualities, the speech of a good poet pours a stream of honey into the ears;

children.text: anadhigataparimalāpi hi harati dṛśaṃ mālatīmālā || 11 ||
children.translated_text: for even without perceiving its fragrance, a garland of <s>mālatī</s> (jasmine) captivates the eye. || 11 ||

children.text: guṇinām api nijarūpapratipattiḥ parata eva saṃbhavati /
children.translated_text: Even for the virtuous, the recognition of one's own nature arises through another;

children.text: svamahimadarśanam akṣṇor mukuratale jāyate yasmāt || 12 ||
children.translated_text: for the vision of one's own greatness is born [only] on the surface of a mirror. || 12 ||

children.text: sarasvatīdattavaraprasādaś cakre subandhuḥ sujanaikabandhuḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Subandhu</s>, the sole friend of the virtuous, blessed by the grace of <s>Sarasvatī</s>,

children.text: pratyakṣaraśleṣamayaprabandhaṃ vinyāsavaidagdhyanidhir nibandham || 13 ||
children.translated_text: a treasury of skill in composition, composed this work (<s>nibandha</s>) consisting of <s>śleṣa</s> (double meaning) in every syllable. || 13 ||

children.text: abhūd abhūtapūrvaḥ, sarvorvīpaticakracūḍāmaṇiśreṇīśāṇakoṇakaṣaṇanirmalīkṛtacaraṇanakhamaṇiḥ, ṇṛsiṃha iva darśitakaśipukṣetradānavismayaḥ, kṛṣṇa iva kṛtavasudevatarpaṇaḥ, nārāyaṇa iva saukaryasamāsāditadharaṇīmaṇḍalaḥ, kaṃsārātir iva janitayaśodānandasamṛddhiḥ, ānakadundubhir iva kṛtakāvyādaraḥ, sāgaraśāyīvānantabhogīcūḍāmaṇirañjitapādaḥ, varuṇa ivāśāntarakṣaṇaḥ, agastya iva dakṣiṇāśāprasādhakaḥ, jalanidhir iva vāhinīśatanāyakaḥ samakarapracāraś ca, hara iva mahāsenānuyāto nirjitamāraś ca, merur iva vibudhālayo viśvakarmāśrayaś ca, ravir iva kṣaṇadānapriyaś cchāyāsantāpaharaś ca, kusumaketur iva janitāniruddhasaṃpad ratisukhapradaś ca, vidyādharo 'pi sumanāḥ, dhṛtarāṣṭro 'pi guṇapriyaḥ, kṣamānugato 'pi sudharmāśritaḥ, bṛhannalānubhāvo 'py antaḥsaralaḥ, mahiṣīsaṃbhavo 'pi vṛṣotpādī, ataralo 'pi mahānāyakaḥ rājā Cintāmaṇir nāma |
children.translated_text: There was one without precedent — a king named <s>Cintāmaṇi</s> — whose toenail-gems were polished bright on the whetstone-edge of the crest-jewel rows of all the earth's overlords; like <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> (the Man-Lion), he displayed wonder by destroying the demon of the field of <s>Kaśipu</s>; like <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, he gratified the deity of wealth (<s>Vasudeva</s>); like <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, he easily obtained the entire earth; like the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, he generated the prosperity and delight of <s>Yaśodā</s> (fame); like <s>Ānakadundubhi</s> (<s>Vasudeva</s>), he honored poetry; like the one who reclines on the ocean, his feet were adorned by the crest-jewel of the serpent <s>Ananta</s>; like <s>Varuṇa</s>, he guarded the quarters; like <s>Agastya</s>, he subdued the southern direction; like the ocean, he was the commander of hundreds of armies and had the movements of a crocodile; like <s>Hara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), he was attended by <s>Mahāsena</s> (<s>Skanda</s>) and had conquered <s>Māra</s>; like <s>Meru</s>, he was the abode of the wise and the refuge of <s>Viśvakarman</s>; like the sun, he was fond of giving in an instant, and removed the suffering of shadow; like the god of love (<s>Kusumaketu</s>), he generated the wealth of <s>Aniruddha</s> and bestowed the pleasure of love; though a <s>Vidyādhara</s> (bearer of knowledge), he was virtuous of mind; though a <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> (firm ruler), he loved merit; though followed by patience, he resorted to righteousness (<s>Sudharma</s>); though of the power of <s>Bṛhannalā</s>, he was straightforward within; though born of a chief queen (<s>mahiṣī</s>), he was a producer of bulls (<s>vṛṣa</s>, i.e. dharma); though not fickle, he was a great leader.

children.text: yatra ca śāsati dharaṇimaṇḍalaṃ chalanigrahaprayogā vādeṣu, nāstikatā cārvākeṣu, kaṇṭakayogo niyogeṣu, parīvādo vīṇāsu, khalasaṃyogaḥ śāliṣu, dvijihvasaṅgṛhītir āhituṇḍikeṣu, kara[cchedaḥ kḷptakara]grahaṇeṣu, netrotpāṭanaṃ munīnāṃ, rājaviruddhatā paṅkajānāṃ, sarvabhaumayogo diggajānāṃ, śūlasaṃyogo yuvatiprasave, agnitulāśuddhiḥ suvarṇānāṃ, duḥśāsanadarśanaṃ bhārate, karapatradāraṇaṃ jalajānāṃ, param evaṃ vyavasthitam | mahāvarāho gotroddharaṇapravṛtto 'pi gotroddalanam akarot | rāghavaḥ pariharann api janakabhuvaṃ janakabhuvā saha vanaṃ viveśa | bharato 'pi rāmadarśitabhaktir api rājye virāmam akarot | nalasya damayantyā militasyāpi punar bhūparigraho jātaḥ | pṛthur api gotrasamutsāraṇād vistāritabhūmaṇḍalaḥ | itthaṃ nāsti vāgavasaraḥ pūrvatararājeṣu |
children.translated_text: And while he ruled the earth: the employment of suppression of deceit [was found only] in debates; atheism only among the <s>Cārvākas</s>; the association with thorns only in mandates (<s>niyoga</s>); censure (<s>parīvāda</s>) only in <s>vīṇās</s> (as a musical term); association with the wicked (<s>khala</s>) only in rice-husking; the seizing of the double-tongued only among snake-charmers; the cutting of hands only in [the ceremony of] grasping the hand [in marriage]; the plucking out of eyes (<s>netrotpāṭana</s>) only among sages [extracting eye-salve]; opposition to the king only among day-lotuses [which close at night]; the yoke of universal sovereignty only among the elephants of the quarters; impalement only in the delivery of young women [difficult childbirth]; trial by fire and scales only for testing gold; the sight of <s>Duḥśāsana</s> only in the <s>Mahābhārata</s>; the cutting with saw-blades only among lotuses [with serrated leaves]. But beyond this, things were thus established: The Great Boar (<s>Mahāvarāha</s>), though engaged in lifting up the <s>gotra</s> (lineage/earth), also split the <s>gotra</s>. <s>Rāghava</s>, though avoiding <s>Janaka</s>'s land, entered the forest with <s>Janaka</s>'s daughter. <s>Bharata</s>, though shown devotion by <s>Rāma</s>, renounced the kingdom. <s>Nala</s>, though united with <s>Damayantī</s>, underwent the seizure of the earth again. <s>Pṛthu</s> extended the sphere of the earth by leveling the mountains (<s>gotra</s>). Thus there is no occasion for speech regarding earlier kings.

children.text:
sa punar anya eva tyaktasarvapūrvorvīpaticaritaḥ | tathā hi | sarvataḥ kaṭakasaṃcāriṇo gandharvān darśitaśṛṅgonnatiḥ sukhayan na virarāma | sa himālayo nāvaśyāyocchalitaḥ no māyājanmane hitaś ca | asau hi mānī giri sthito vṛṣadhvajaś ca | [asau] sadgatiḥ, avadhūtākhilakāntāraḥ, pāvakāgresaraḥ, na bhogotsukaḥ sumanoharaḥ[ś ca] | sa ratnākaro 'nahimayaḥ, katham agādhaḥ, samaryādaḥ, nodreko 'py asya vismayaḥ, himakarāśrayo 'mṛtamayaḥ, satpātraḥ, tasyācalo na krodhaḥ, mahānadīnaḥ, sapotaḥ sa samudraḥ | [sa candra iva] kṣaṇadānandakaraḥ, kumudavanabandhuḥ, sakalakalākulagṛhaṃ, natārātibalaḥ | [sa samudro] mitrodayahetuḥ, kāñcana śobhāṃ bibhrat, acalādhikalakṣmīḥ sumerur iva | yasya ca ripuvargaḥ sadā pārtho 'pi na mahābhārataraṇayogyaḥ, bhīṣmo 'py aśāntanave hitaḥ, sānucaro 'pi na gotrabhūṣitaḥ | api ca sa triśaṅkur iva nakṣatrapathasthalitaḥ, śaṅkaro 'pi na viṣādī, pāvako 'pi na kṛṣṇavartmā, āśrayāśo ['pi] na dahanaḥ, nāntaka ivākasmād apahṛtajīvanaḥ, na rāhur mitramaṇḍalagrahaṇavardhitaruciḥ, na nala iva kalivilasitavinaṭitaḥ, na cakrīva śṛgālavadhastutisamullasitaḥ, nandagopa iva yaśodayānvitaḥ, jarāsandha iva ghaṭitasandhivigrahaḥ, bhārgava iva sadānabhogaḥ, daśaratha iva sumitropetaḥ sumantrādhiṣṭhitaś ca, dilīpa iva sudakṣiṇānugato rakṣitaguś ca, rāma iva janitakuśalavayo rūpocchrāyaḥ | tasya ca pārijāta ivāśritanandanaḥ, himālaya iva janitaśivaḥ, mandara iva bhogibhogāṅkitaḥ, kailāsa iva maheśvaropabhuktakoṭiḥ, madhur iva nānārāmānandakaraḥ, kṣīrodamathanodyatamandara iva mukharitabhuvanaḥ, rāgarajjur ivollāsitaratiḥ, īśānabhūtisañcaya iva sandhyocchalitaḥ, śaranmegha ivāvadātahṛdayo viṣṇupadāvalambī ca, pārtha iva samarasāhasocitaḥ, kaṃsa iva kuvalayāpīḍabhūṣitaḥ, tārkṣya iva [vinatānandakaraḥ] sumukhanandana[ś ca], viṣṇur iva kroḍīkṛtasutanuḥ, śāntanava iva svavaśasthāpitakāladharmaḥ, kauravavyūha iva suśarmādhiṣṭhitaḥ, subāhur api rāmānandī, samadṛṣṭir api maheśvaro, muktāmayo 'py ataralamadhyo,
jalada iva vimalataravāridhārātrāsitarājahaṃsaḥ, vaṃśapradīpo 'py akṣatadaśaḥ, tanayaḥ Kandarpaketur nāma |
children.translated_text: He, however, was quite different, having surpassed the conduct of all previous kings. For: he delighted the <s>Gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians) roaming everywhere in his encampments, having displayed the elevation of his peak — he, the <s>Himālaya</s>, was not caused by frost nor born of illusion, but beneficial. He was a proud mountain, standing firm, bearing the bull-banner [of <s>Śiva</s>]. He was of noble course, having cast off all wilderness; fire went before him, yet he was not eager for enjoyment, but charming of mind. He was a mine of jewels, yet not cold; how unfathomable, yet within bounds! His wonder had no excess. He was the abode of the moon, full of nectar, a worthy vessel. His immovability was not anger. He was [like] great rivers, with boats — that ocean. Like the moon, he brought delight in moments of giving; friend of the lotus-groves; his home was full of all arts; the strength of his enemies bowed down. [Like the ocean,] he was the cause of his friend's rise; bearing golden splendor; possessing more beauty than mountains — like <s>Sumeru</s>. His enemy host, even though a <s>Pārtha</s> (warrior), was never fit to cross the great [ocean of] battle; his <s>Bhīṣma</s>, though [terrifying], was devoted to the son of <s>Śāntanu</s>; his retinue, though with followers, was not adorned with mere clan-pride. Moreover, he, like <s>Triśaṅku</s>, was established on the stellar path; though a <s>Śaṅkara</s>, he was not despondent; though a fire, he did not follow the dark path; though a refuge of hope, he was not a conflagration; not like Death, suddenly snatching lives; not like <s>Rāhu</s>, whose splendor increases by seizing the circle of the sun; not like <s>Nala</s>, whose dignity was ruined by <s>Kali's</s> sport; not like the <s>Cakrin</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>), delighted by praise for slaying a jackal; like <s>Nandagopa</s>, accompanied by <s>Yaśodā</s> (fame); like <s>Jarāsandha</s>, skilled in joining war and peace; like <s>Bhārgava</s> (<s>Paraśurāma</s>), ever without [desire for] enjoyment; like <s>Daśaratha</s>, accompanied by <s>Sumitrā</s> (good friendship) and guided by <s>Sumantra</s> (good counsel); like <s>Dilīpa</s>, followed by <s>Sudakṣiṇā</s> (good generosity) and a protector of cows; like <s>Rāma</s>, who raised <s>Kuśa</s> and <s>Lava</s>, exalted in beauty. His son, named <s>Kandarpaketu</s>, was like the <s>Pārijāta</s> tree — a refuge of delight; like the <s>Himālaya</s> — begetter of <s>Śiva's</s> [bride]; like <s>Mandara</s> — marked by the coils of serpents; like <s>Kailāsa</s> — whose peak was enjoyed by <s>Maheśvara</s>; like <s>Mathurā</s> — delighting with various gardens; like <s>Mandara</s> raised for churning the milk-ocean — making the world resound; like the cord of passion — arousing delight; like a collection of <s>Īśāna's</s> wealth — rising up at twilight; like an autumn cloud — of pure heart and clinging to the path of <s>Viṣṇu</s>; like <s>Pārtha</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>) — accustomed to the boldness of battle; like <s>Kaṃsa</s> — adorned with the elephant <s>Kuvalayāpīḍa</s>; like <s>Tārkṣya</s> (<s>Garuḍa</s>) — bringing joy to <s>Vinatā</s> and son of <s>Sumukha</s>; like <s>Viṣṇu</s> — who embraced the slender-bodied one; like <s>Śāntanava</s> (<s>Bhīṣma</s>) — who established the law of time by his own will; like a <s>Kaurava</s> formation — commanded by <s>Suśarman</s>; though fair-armed, a lover of <s>Rāma</s>; though even-sighted, a great lord; though made of pearls, steady at the center; like a rain-cloud, frightening the royal geese with his streams of exceedingly pure water; a lamp of his lineage yet with undiminished faculties.

children.text: yena ca candreṇeva sakalakalākulagṛheṇa, śarvarītihāriṇā, kumudavanabandhunā, prasāditāśena, vilokitā jaladhaya ivollasitagotrāḥ, sudūravartitajīvanāḥ, prasannasattvāḥ santaḥ parām ṛddhim avāpuḥ prajālokāḥ | yasya ca janitāniruddhalīlasya, ratipriyasya, kusumaśarāsanasya, makaraketor iva darśanena vanitājanasya hṛdayam ullalāsa | yasmai cānugatadakṣiṇasadāgataye, netraśrutisukhadakomalakokilarutāya, vikāsitapallavāya, kṛtakāntārataraṅgāya, surabhisumano'bhirāmāya, sarvajanasulabhapadmāya, vistṛtakarasaṃpade, atikrāntadamanakāya vasantāyeva, vanalatā ivotkalikāsahasrasaṃkulāḥ, bhramarasaṅgatāḥ, pravālahāriṇyaḥ, vilasadvayasas taruṇyaḥ spṛhayāṃcakruḥ | yasya [ca] samarabhuvi bhujadaṇḍena kodaṇḍaṃ, kodaṇḍena bāṇāḥ, bānai ripuśiraḥ, tenāpi bhūmaṇḍalaṃ, tena cānanubhūtapūrvo nāyakaḥ, nāyakena ca kīrtiḥ, kīrtyā ca saptasāgarāḥ, sāgaraiḥ kṛtayugādi rājacaritasmaraṇaṃ, anena ca sthairyaṃ, amunā ca pratikṣaṇam āścaryam āsāditam | yasya ca pratāpānaladagdhānāṃ ripusundarīṇāṃ karatalatāḍanabhītair iva muktāhāraiḥ payodharaparisaro muktaḥ | yasya ca nihitanārācajarjaritamattamātaṅgakumbhasthalavigalitamuktāphaladanturitaparisare, taratpatrarathe, raktavārisaṃcaratkarikacchapotphullapuṇḍarīkaśatasamākule, nṛtyatkabandhe, surasundarīsaṃgamotsukacārabhaṭāhaṅkārasaṃbhārabhīṣaṇe, samarasarasi, bhinnapadātikarituragarudhirārdro jayalakṣmīpādālaktakarāgarañjita iva khaḍgo rarāja |
children.translated_text: And by him — who, like the moon, had a household full of all arts (<s>kalā</s>, also: lunar digits), who dispelled the darkness of night, who was a friend of the night-lily groves, who satisfied all directions — looked upon [by him], the people attained supreme prosperity, just as the oceans, with their uplifted mountain-ranges (also: exalted lineages), with far-reaching rivers (also: livelihoods), with tranquil creatures (also: clear-natured), [are graced by the moonlight]. And by the sight of him — whose sport was as irresistible as <s>Aniruddha</s>'s, who was dear to <s>Rati</s> (love), who bore a flower-bow like <s>Kāmadeva</s>, who had the <s>makara</s> (sea-monster) as his emblem — the hearts of young women were set dancing. And to him — like unto the Spring (<s>Vasanta</s>), ever approaching with gracious generosity, whose soft cuckoo-song was pleasing to the eye and ear, who unfolded blossoms, who made the forest-depths ripple with waves, who delighted with fragrant flowers, whose lotus-feet were accessible to all, whose wealth of hand was expansive, who surpassed even the <s>damanaka</s> (amaranth, also: self-restraint) — young women in the bloom of youth, like forest-creepers swarming with thousands of buds, accompanied by bees, stealing with fresh shoots, yearned [for him]. And on the battlefield, by his arm the bow was wielded; by the bow, arrows [were launched]; by the arrows, the heads of enemies [were severed]; by them, the earth was [conquered]; by that, a hero never before experienced [arose]; by the hero, fame [was won]; by fame, the seven seas [were reached]; by the seas, the memory of royal exploits from the <s>Kṛta Yuga</s> onward [was evoked]; by this, steadfastness [was attained]; and by that, wonder was produced at every moment. And the breasts of the enemy's beautiful women, scorched by the fire of his valor, were abandoned by their pearl necklaces, as if the pearls had fled in fear of being struck by their hands [in grief]. And his sword shone splendid in the lake of battle — whose shores were strewn with pearls trickling from the temple-globes of maddened elephants pierced and shattered by iron arrows, where chariots bobbed like leaves, where hundreds of lotuses bloomed as red [with blood] waters where the elephant-young of war-elephants waded, where headless trunks danced, terrifying with the clamor and pride of heroic warriors eager for the embrace of celestial maidens — wet with the blood of slain foot-soldiers, elephants, and horses, his sword appeared as if painted red with the <s>alaktaka</s> (lac-dye) from the feet of the goddess of Victory (<s>Jayalakṣmī</s>).

children.translated_text: Then, as if drinking her in with his gaze expanded by delight, he was released by sleep — as if by jealousy — which had long attended him. But having awoken, like one immersed in a pool of poison, like one [immersed] in the words of wicked men, he could not ascertain himself. For a moment, his arms spread out as if to embrace the vault of the sky, he called to his beloved in the directions and intermediate directions: "Come, come, dearest! Do not go, do not go!" — as if she were inscribed [in the quarters], as if engraved [there], as if embedded in his eye, as if fixed in his heart. children.translated_text: Then his dear friend named <s>Makaranda</s>, having somehow gained entry, spoke to <s>Kandarpaketu</s> who was helpless from the blow of <s>Kandarpa</s>'s (Love's) arrow: "Friend, why have you adopted this improper behavior befitting wicked people? The shoots of wicked vices arise without seed, spread without occasion, and become difficult to uproot. For a particle of fault, having entered the heart of the wicked, grows terrible, while it does not even enter the heart of the good; and if by some chance it does enter, then like mercury it does not stay even for a moment. Like deer, the good become weary from the drops of [sweat from] exertion. People like you easily charm like the autumn season, but they do not give improper counsel to a conscious friend. Even the friendship of unconscious things is placed in a fitting quarter. For instance, water, thinking 'since milk — which has gained renown through its sweetness, coolness, and purity, and whose peace from torment was increased by contact with me — is being boiled, it is proper that I should diminish first before it,' itself diminishes. So this conduct is improper. Friend, take the path befitting good people. For good people go astray only through delusion" — and so on. While he was speaking thus, <s>Kandarpaketu</s>, though overpowered by the blow of <s>Smara</s> (Love), spoke in measured words: "Dear friend, like <s>Diti</s>, the mental disposition of the good is agitated by a hundred afflictions. This is not the time for advice. My limbs seem to be burning, my senses seem to be boiling, my vital parts seem to be splitting, my breaths seem to be departing, my powers of discrimination seem to be uprooted, my memory seems lost. If you are now one who shared my childhood games and shares equally my sorrows and joys, then follow me" — having said this, unnoticed by his attendants, he left the city with him.

whose rock surfaces were perfumed by breezes carrying the fragrance of flowing <s>haricandana</s> (yellow sandalwood) broken and dragged by the trunks of mountain elephants; with troops of monkeys eager to taste the palmyra fruit juice moistening their palms from fruits broken by falling from great heights; like a lover, accompanied by the passionate sentiment of wilderness-anger and full of intoxication; like <s>Śrīparvata</s>, with <s>Mallikārjuna</s> nearby; like <s>Naravāhanadatta</s>, with <s>Priyaṅguśyāmā</s> as its mistress; like an infant, held by a nurse (<s>dhātrī</s>/myrobalan tree); like the beginning of day, with its rows of leaf-forests reddened by the dawn's radiance; like the dark fortnight, dense with abundant creepers; like <s>Karṇa</s>, having experienced the giving of hundreds of millions; like <s>Bhīṣma</s>, adorned with half-moons released by <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s>; like the arrangement of the <s>Kāmasūtra</s>, delighted by the passion of wrestling elephants fitted together in the wilderness; children.translated_text: And [the mountain] which, through its dense thickets, displayed many mineral transformations visible here — like a saint (<s>sādhu</s>) whose greatness is revealed through compassionate conduct; like <s>Mīmāṃsā</s> logic, concealing the Digambara (Jain) view. And which was adorned at its borders by pools — delightful with the appearance of lotuses like [episodes of] the <s>Harivaṃśa</s>, teeming with fish, paired crabs, and tortoises like zodiac signs (<s>rāśi</s>), accompanied by birds, serpents, auspicious figures, and <s>bakula</s> trees like astronomical instruments (<s>karaṇa</s>). And which displayed the play of many meters (<s>vṛtta</s>) through its creepers — colorful with blossoms, with leaves fallen from bamboo, delicately graceful, flowering at their tips, peaked like <s>Śikhariṇī</s> [meter], delightful like <s>Praharṣiṇī</s> [meter]. And which was embraced by the <s>Revā</s> (Narmadā) river, like a beloved extending her wave-arms — whose waters were perfumed by clusters of honey-drops trickling from fragments of open lotuses shaken by the gorgeous fanning tails of cranes, geese, and <s>sārasa</s> birds intoxicated with passion; whose waters were drunk by circles of navels of royal beauties emerging at evening time; whose shores and sandbanks resounded with the clamor of flocks of regal swans trumpeting in passion; whose waters were streaked by streams of ichor flowing from the temple-globes of maddened elephants along the banks; whose groves along the shore bore witness to the amorous play of young divine couples comfortably seated on sand-beds formed by clumps of dust fallen from the <s>ketakī</s> (screwpine) groves growing on the banks; whose waters were bathed in by river-goddesses stationed in pavilions of <s>jambū</s> (rose-apple) groves fallen near the bank-hollows; whose pleasures were partaken by divine couples drawn by curiosity at the passionate cooing calls of flocks of <s>dātyūha</s> (gallinule) birds hidden within the <s>vetasa</s> (cane) creepers growing on the banks; whose shores echoed with the gurgling cries of potter-bird (<s>kulāla</s>) and rooster flocks born near the bank; whose soft sandbanks were trodden by water-creatures; whose waves rippled, swayed by the breeze from the groves; whose half-visible fish (<s>śaphara</s>) were watched by families of crane-hens nesting in clusters of reed-thickets; whose <s>vetasa</s> (cane) forests were fearsome with stakes and <s>koyaṣṭi</s> (kingfisher) poles of fishermen greedy for catches; whose near-shore waters were graced by darting, swift rows of <s>pāla</s> fish visible between garlands of waves; whose banks were being dug by hundreds of <s>kirāta</s> (tribal) people curious to find buried treasure revealed by the mating of <s>khañjarīṭa</s> (wagtail) pairs — as if angry, showing grimaces; as if intoxicated, stumbling in gait; like the beauty of dawn, with swelling tides; like the battlefield of the <s>Bhārata</s> war, with dancing headless trunks; like the rainy season, with spreading hundred-petaled [lotuses] concealing poison-bearers; like desire for wealth, performing service to mountains (<s>bhūbhṛt</s>) — by the <s>Revā</s>, like a beloved extending her wave-arms in embrace.

who, like <s>Garuḍa</s>, caused burning in the hearts of the amorous; who, like a blind demon, were impaled upon spears (also: frequented spear-points) — [such was] the city called <s>Kusumapura</s>.

children.text: yatra ca surāsuramaulimaṇimālālālitacaraṇāravindā, śumbhaniśumbhabalamahāvanadāvānalajvālā, mahiṣamahāsuragirivaravajradhārā, praṇayapraṇatagaṅgādharajaṭājūṭaskhalitajāhnavījaladhārādhautapādapadmā bhagavatī Kātyāyanī Caṇḍābhidhānā svayaṃ nivasati | yasya parisare surāsuramukuṭakusumarajorājiparimalavāhinī, prajāpatikamaṇḍaludharmadravadhārā, dharātalagatasagarasutaśatasuranagarasamārohaṇapuṇyarajjuḥ, airāvaṇakaṭakamaṭhakampitataṭā, haricandanasyandanasurabhitasalilā salīlasurasundarīnitambabimbāhatitaralitataraṅgā, snānāvatīrṇasaptarṣimālāvimalajaṭāṭavīparimalapuṇyaveṇiḥ, eṇatilakamukuṭajaṭājūṭakuharabhrāntijanitasaṃskāratayaiva kuṭilāvartā, dharaṇīva sārvabhaumakarasparśopabhogakṣamā, jaladakālasarasīva gandhāndhoparibhramadbhramaramālānumīyamānajalamagnakumudapuṇḍarīkā, chandovicitir iva mālinīsanāthā, grahapaṅktir iva sūryātmajopaśobhitā sarājahaṃsā ca, śaratkāladinaśrīr ivojjvalatkokanadā prabuddhapuṇḍarīkākṣā ca, hatāndhatamasāpi tamasānvitā, [vīcikalitāpy avīcidurgamā] bhagavatī Bhāgarathī pravahati |
children.translated_text: And there, the blessed <s>Kātyāyanī</s>, named <s>Caṇḍā</s>, herself resides — whose lotus-feet are caressed by the jeweled diadems of gods and demons, who is a forest-fire to the great forest of the army of <s>Śumbha</s> and <s>Niśumbha</s>, who is a thunderbolt-stream upon the great mountain of the buffalo-demon (<s>Mahiṣāsura</s>), whose lotus-feet are washed by the streams of <s>Jāhnavī</s>'s (Ganges') waters cascading from the matted locks of <s>Gaṅgādhara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) who bows lovingly before her. In her vicinity flows the blessed <s>Bhāgīrathī</s> (Ganges) — carrying the fragrance of the pollen-dust from the flower-garlands on the crowns of gods and demons; a stream of the liquid of dharma from the water-vessel of <s>Prajāpati</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>); a sacred rope for the hundreds of sons of <s>Sagara</s> lying upon the earth to ascend to the city of the gods; whose banks are shaken by the tortoise-shaped temples of <s>Airāvaṇa</s> (Indra's elephant); whose waters are perfumed by divine <s>haricandana</s> (sandalwood) chariots; whose waves are set dancing by the playful swaying of the hips of celestial maidens bathing; whose sacred braid is fragrant with the matted forests of hair of the seven sages who have descended for a bath; whose winding eddies appear as if made curving by the training acquired from whirling about in the caves of the matted locks of <s>Śiva</s> crowned with the crescent moon — like the earth, capable of bearing the touch and enjoyment of a universal sovereign (<s>sārvabhauma</s>); like a pool in the rainy season, with lotuses inferred from the garlands of bees circling above, blinded by fragrance, over submerged water-lilies and lotuses; like a composition in varied meter (<s>chandoviciti</s>), graced by the <s>Mālinī</s> (meter/garland); like a row of planets, adorned by the son of the Sun (<s>Śani</s>, also: royal swans); and like the beauty of an autumn day, with brilliant red lotuses (<s>kokanada</s>) and awakened lotuses (<s>puṇḍarīka</s>) — though the darkness has been destroyed, she is still accompanied by <s>Tamasā</s> (a river, also: darkness); though having waves, she is hard to access without the infernal region (<s>Avīci</s>, also: without waves).

children.translated_text: pole; whose thousands of tender new shoots were produced by the sprinkling of ambrosia-drops transmitted from the beautiful feet of the army of the moon — [trees] like the exploits of <s>Bharata</s>, always dwelling in lovely groves; like great heroes, bearing coconut-palms (also: bearing the breast-pots); like unrefined youths, with far-extended eyes (also: branches); like ascetics, devoted to <s>japā</s> (prayer, also: the hibiscus plant); like adorned [women], beautified with garlands; like lions risen to split the temple-globes of elephants, with erect manes (also: ears of grain); though associated with <s>ariṣṭa</s> (the soapberry tree, also: misfortune), long-lived; though accompanied by sages (<s>muni</s>, also: the agati tree), presided over by <s>Madana</s> (Love) — the [city was] adorned [by these], like the womb of <s>Aditi</s>, inhabited by many temples of the gods (also: many gods); like the netherworld (<s>Pātāla</s>), graced by <s>Mahābali</s> and inhabited by serpents; though purified by temples of the gods (also: divine liquor), undisturbed by the serpent-kings (also: enjoyers).

children.text: tatra ca suratabharakhinnasuptasīmantinīratnatāṭaṅkamudrāṅkitabāhudaṇḍaḥ, pracaṇḍapratipakṣalakṣmīkeśapāśakusumamālāmodasurabhitakarakamalaḥ, praśastakedāra iva bahudhānyakāryasaṃpādakaḥ, pārtha iva subhadrānvitaḥ sabhīmasenaś ca, kṛṣṇa iva satyabhāmopetaḥ Śṛṅgāraśekharo nāma rājā prativasati | yo balabhit pāvako dharmarāṇ nirṛtiḥ pracetāḥ sadāgatir dhanadaḥ śaṅkara ity aṣṭamūrtir apy anaṣṭamūrtiḥ |
children.translated_text: And there dwells a king named <s>Śṛṅgāraśekhara</s> — whose arm-staff bore the imprint of jeweled ear-ornaments of women asleep, exhausted from love-making; whose lotus-hand was fragrant with the perfume of the flower-garlands from the hair-braids of the fortune (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) of his fierce adversaries; like a renowned rice-field (<s>kedāra</s>, also: <s>Kedāra</s>), accomplishing many grain-works (also: auspicious deeds); like <s>Pārtha</s> (<s>Arjuna</s>), accompanied by <s>Subhadrā</s> and together with <s>Bhīmasena</s>; like <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, accompanied by <s>Satyabhāmā</s>. He who is <s>Balabhit</s> (<s>Indra</s>, slayer of Bala), <s>Pāvaka</s> (Fire), <s>Dharmarāj</s> (<s>Yama</s>), <s>Nirṛti</s>, <s>Pracetas</s> (<s>Varuṇa</s>), <s>Sadāgati</s> (<s>Vāyu</s>), <s>Dhanada</s> (<s>Kubera</s>), and <s>Śaṅkara</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) — though eight-formed, his form was not destroyed (also: he embodied the eight guardians of the directions while remaining undiminished).

children.translated_text: His hand bears the affection of a hundred <s>koṭis</s> (crores); he, the giver of all possessions, conquers the lord of the gods (<s>Sureśa</s>, i.e. <s>Indra</s>) as if [he were but] a blade of grass. || 17 ||

children.text: jīvākṛṣṭiṃ sa cakre mṛdhabhuvi dhanuṣaḥ śatrur āsīd gatāsur lakṣāptir mārgaṇānām abhavad aribale tad yaśas tena labdham /
children.translated_text: On the battlefield he performed the attraction of life [from his enemies]; his foe became lifeless through the bow; the arrows achieved their mark in the enemy's army; by that, fame was obtained;

children.text: muktā tena kṣameti tvaritam arigaṇair uttamāṅgaiḥ pratīṣṭo pañcatvaṃ dveṣisainye sthitam avanipatir nāpa saṅkhyāntaraṃ saḥ || 18 ||
children.translated_text: Pearls (also: liberation) were released by him [from enemy heads]; quickly by the enemy hordes with their severed heads he was worshipped; destruction (<s>pañcatva</s>) stood firm in the enemy army — that king did not attain any other number [than one, i.e. he was peerless]. || 18 ||

children.text: yatra ca rājanīticature caturambudhimekhalāyā bhuvo nāyake śāsati vasumatīṃ pitṛkārye vṛṣotsargaḥ, śaśinaḥ kanyātulārohaḥ, yogeṣu śūlaghātādicintā, dakṣiṇavāmakaraṇaṃ digviniścayeṣu, śarabhedo dadhiṣu, śṛṅkhalābandho varṇagrathanāsu, utprekṣāṣepaḥ kāvyālaṅkāreṣu, lakṣadānacyutiḥ sāyakānāṃ, kvipāṃ sarvavināśaḥ, kośasaṅkocaḥ kamalākareṣu, jātihīnatā duṣkuleṣu na puṣpamālāsu, śṛṅgārahānir jaratkariṣu na janeṣu, durvarṇayogaḥ kambikādiṣu na kāminīkāntiṣu, gāndhāravicchedo rāgeṣu na pauravanitāsu, mūrcchādhigamo gāneṣu, kharmābhāvo nīcasevakeṣu na paridhāneṣu, malināmbaratvaṃ niśāsu na janeṣu, calarāgatā gīteṣu na vidagdhajaneṣu, vṛṣahāniḥ nidhuvanalīlāsu na paureṣu, bhaṅguratvaṃ rāgavikṛtiṣu na citteṣu, anaṅgatā kāmadeve na parijane, mārāgamo yauvanodayeṣu na prakṛtiṣu, dvijaghātaḥ surateṣu na prajāsu, raśanābandho ratikalaheṣu na dānānumatiṣu, adhararāgatā taruṇīṣu na parijaneṣu, kartanam alakabhrūṣu na purandhrīṣu, nistriṃśatvam asīnāṃ, karavālanāśo yodhānāṃ paraṃ vyavasthitaḥ |
children.translated_text: And where, while that king skilled in statecraft (<s>rājanīti</s>) ruled the earth girdled by four oceans — the release of bulls (<s>vṛṣotsarga</s>) occurred only in ancestral rites [not as a sign of abandoned dharma]; the rising of the maiden to the scales (<s>kanyātulāroha</s>) occurred only for the moon [the zodiac sign Libra, not as a weighing of brides]; thoughts of impalement (<s>śūlaghāta</s>) occurred only in yoga [not as punishment]; the 'right-and-left operation' (<s>dakṣiṇa-vāma-karaṇa</s>) occurred only in determining directions [not as injustice]; the splitting of arrows (<s>śarabheda</s>) occurred only in curds [not in warfare]; the chaining (<s>śṛṅkhalābandha</s>) occurred only in stringing syllables together [not as imprisonment]; the charge of extravagant fancy (<s>utprekṣā-kṣepa</s>) occurred only in poetic ornament [not as false accusation]; the fall of a hundred thousand targets (<s>lakṣa-dāna-cyuti</s>) occurred only for arrows [not as loss of charity]; the total destruction of <s>kvip</s> occurred only [as a grammatical suffix, not as ruin]; the contraction of the treasury (<s>kośa-saṅkoca</s>) occurred only in lotus-pools [not in state finances]; loss of caste (<s>jāti-hīnatā</s>) occurred only in lowly families, not in flower-garlands; the loss of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment) occurred only in old elephants (<s>jaratkarin</s>), not in people; the joining of ill-color (<s>durvarṇa-yoga</s>) occurred only in [grammatical forms like] <s>kambikā</s>, not in the beauty of women; the break of <s>gāndhāra</s> [the musical note] occurred only in <s>rāgas</s> (musical modes), not in the city-women; the attainment of <s>mūrcchā</s> (fainting, also: a musical scale) occurred only in songs; absence of joy (<s>kharma</s>) occurred only in lowly servants, not in garments; the state of soiled clothing (<s>malīnāmbaratva</s>) occurred only at night [when darkness 'soils' the sky], not in people; fickleness of passion (<s>calarāgatā</s>) occurred only in songs, not in refined persons; loss of virility (<s>vṛṣa-hāni</s>) occurred only in love-sport [the zodiac sign Taurus], not in citizens; fragility (<s>bhaṅguratva</s>) occurred only in the modifications of passion, not in minds; bodylessness (<s>anaṅgatā</s>) occurred only for <s>Kāmadeva</s> (the bodiless god of love), not in the retinue; the coming of <s>Māra</s> (death/temptation) occurred only at the onset of youth, not among the subjects; the slaying of the twice-born (<s>dvija-ghāta</s>) occurred only in love-making [the biting of teeth], not among the people; the tying of girdles (<s>raśanā-bandha</s>) occurred only in love-quarrels, not in the granting of permissions; redness of lips (<s>adhara-rāgatā</s>) occurred only in young women, not in the retinue [as a sign of drinking]; cutting (<s>kartana</s>) occurred only of hair-locks and eyebrows, not of [respectable] women; the state of being swordlike (<s>nistriṃśatva</s>) occurred only for swords; and the destruction of the hand-sword occurred only among warriors — thus was the settled order.

children.text: tasya ca mahiṣī diggajamadalekhevānanditālimālā, pārvatīva sukumārā candralekhālaṅkṛtā ca, vanarājir iva navamālikodbhāsitā sacitrakā ca, apsarassaṃhatir iva saṃhatasukeśī samañjughoṣā ca, sarvāntaḥpurapradhānabhūtā Anaṅgavatī nāma | tayoś ca madhyamopāntavayasi vartamānayoḥ katham api daiva(va)śāt tribhuvanavilobhanīyākṛtiḥ, pulomatanayevānanditasahasranetrā Vāsavadattā nāma [tanayā] babhūva | atha sā rāvaṇabhujavana ivollāsitagotreva pariṇāmam upayāty api yauvanabhāve pariṇayaparaṅmukhī tasthau |
children.translated_text: And his chief queen — like a streak of rut-fluid from a direction-elephant, delighting garlands of bees; like <s>Pārvatī</s>, delicate and adorned with a crescent-moon mark; like a line of forest trees, radiant with fresh <s>mālatī</s> (jasmine) and accompanied by <s>citraka</s> (the variegated one, also: a tree); like a group of <s>apsarases</s> (celestial nymphs), with beautifully gathered hair and melodious sounds — [this queen], foremost of all the women of the inner palace, was named <s>Anaṅgavatī</s>. And to the two of them, when they were in the middle to latter part of their youth, somehow by the will of fate, a daughter was born named <s>Vāsavadattā</s> — whose form was captivating to all three worlds, who delighted the thousand-eyed one (<s>Indra</s>) like the daughter of <s>Puloman</s> (<s>Śacī</s>). Then she, though coming to maturity in youthful state — like the arm-forest of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, with uplifted lineage (also: uplifted Gotra mountain) — remained averse to marriage.

children.text: athaikadā tu vijṛmbhamāṇasahakārakorakanikurumbanipatitamadhukaramālāmadahuṅkārajanitapathikasaṃjvaraḥ, komalamalayamārutodbhūtacūtaprasavasarasāsvādakaṣāyakaṇṭhakalakaṇṭhakuharitabharitasakaladiṅmukhaḥ, vikacakamalakhaṇḍalīyamānamattakalahaṃsakulakolāhalamukharitakamalasarovaraḥ, parabhṛtanakhakoṭipāṭitapāṭalakuḍmalavivaravinirgatamadhudhārāsāraśīkarakaṇanikarasamārabdhadakṣiṇasamīrabāṇadurvraṇitapathikavadhūhṛdayaḥ, madhumadamuditakāminīgaṇḍūṣasīdhusekapulakitabakulaḥ, madanarayaparavaśavikāsinītulākoṭivikaṭacaṭulacaraṇāravindāmandaprahārahṛṣṭakaṅkeliśataḥ, pratidiśam aślīlaprāyagīyamānaśravaṇotsukakhiṅgajanaprāyaprārabdhacarcarīgītākarṇanamuhyadanekapathikaśataḥ, durjana iva satāmarasaḥ, duṣkula iva jātihīnaḥ, rāvaṇa ivāpītalohitapalāśaśatasevitaḥ, mahāśṛṅgārīva sugandhavahaḥ, surājeva samṛddhakuvalayaḥ, vāstavika iva vardhitasukhāśaḥ, satkavikāvyabandha ivābaddhatuhīnaḥ, satpuruṣa iva doṣānubandharahitaḥ, kaivarta iva baddharājīvotpalamālaḥ, samṛddhakāsāraśakunisārtha iva ninditamaruvakaḥ, śakra ivendrāṇīrucitaḥ, mahāvīra ivādharīkṛtadamanakaḥ, khiṅga ivāmlānasubhago vasantakāla ājagāma |
children.translated_text: Then one day, the springtime (<s>vasantakāla</s>) arrived — causing fever in travelers by the humming intoxication of bee-garlands falling upon clusters of bursting mango buds; filling all directions with the cooing of <s>kokilas</s> (cuckoos) whose throats were astringent from tasting the sap of mango blossoms borne by the gentle Malaya breeze; making the lotus-lakes resound with the clamor of flocks of intoxicated graceful swans hovering over fields of blooming lotuses; wounding the hearts of travelers' wives with the arrows of the southern breeze, whose spray-drops were the shower of honey-streams issuing from the openings of <s>pāṭala</s> (trumpet-flower) buds split by the claw-tips of <s>parabḥṛta</s> (cuckoo) birds; causing <s>bakula</s> (mimusops) trees to bristle with horripilation from the sprinkling of mouthfuls of wine by women intoxicated with the madness of spring; [a time] when hundreds of <s>kaṅkeli</s> (aśoka) trees were delighted by the not-so-gentle kicks of the restless lotus-feet of women overpowered by the arrows of <s>Madana</s> (the god of love) in the abundance of blossoms; causing hundreds of travelers to swoon upon hearing the <s>carcarī</s> songs begun mostly by <s>khiṅga</s> birds (also: eunuchs) eager-eared for the mostly indecent songs being sung in every direction — [the spring] like a wicked person, hostile to good men (also: having lotuses as enemies); like one of low birth, devoid of caste (also: devoid of <s>jāti</s> jasmine); like <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, attended by hundreds of pale-red <s>palāśa</s> leaves (also: by those who have drunk blood); like a great lover (<s>mahāśṛṅgārī</s>), bearing fragrant breezes; like a good kingdom, abounding in water-lilies (<s>kuvalaya</s>, also: abundant earth); like a real [thing], increasing the hope of happiness; like the work of a true poet, unfettered by quivers (also: free from the tuhīna/frost); like a virtuous person, free from the connection of faults (also: the night); like a fisherman, with bound garlands of lotuses and blue lilies; like a flock of rich <s>kāsāra</s> birds, disparaging the <s>maruvaka</s> (desert plants); like <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>), delighted by <s>Indrāṇī</s> (also: the Indrāṇī plant); like a great hero, having subdued the <s>damanaka</s> (amaranth, also: self-restraint); like a <s>khiṅga</s> bird, unfadingly beautiful.

children.text: atidūrapravṛddhena madhunā jagati ko vā na vikriyate yad atimukto 'pi munir api vicakāsa | kusumaśarasya navacūtaśaramūlanilīnamadhukarāvali patreṇeva reje | vṛntanirgatavicakilavivare guñjanmadhukaro makaraketos tribhuvanavijayaśaṅkhadhvanim iva cakāra | navayāvakapaṅkapallavitasanūpurataruṇīcaraṇaprahārānurāgavaśān navakisalayacchalena tam eva rāgam udavahad aśokapādapaḥ | madhuramadhudhvanitakāminīmukhakamalasaṅgānurāgād iva tadrasam ātmakusumeṣu bibhrad bakulatarū rarājata | antarāntarānipatitamadhukaranikarakirmīraḥ kaṅkeliguccho 'rdhanirvāṇamanobhavacitācakrānukārī pathikajanadāham uvāha | vikacavicakilarājir alikulaśabalendranīlamuktāvalīva madhuśriyo ruruce | virahiṇīhṛdayamathanāya kusumaśarasya cakram iva nāgakesarakusumam aśobhata | pathikahṛdayam astyaṃ grahītuṃ makaraketoḥ palāva iva pāṭalipuṣpam adaśyata |
children.translated_text: Who in this world is not transformed by the honey (spring) that has spread excessively far? For even the <s>atimukta</s> (jasmine, literally 'the fully liberated one') — even a sage — blossomed forth. The arrow of the flower-armed god (<s>Kāma</s>) shone with its leaf-like rows of bees concealed at the base of the fresh mango shaft. In the opening of the stalk where a bee hummed within the bud, the bee produced a sound like the conch of victory over the three worlds blown by the banner-bearer of the <s>makara</s> (<s>Kāmadeva</s>). The <s>aśoka</s> tree, through passion born of the blows of the feet of young women adorned with tinkling anklets and reddened with fresh <s>yāvaka</s> (lac-paste), bore under the pretext of fresh shoots that very same redness. The <s>bakula</s> tree shone resplendent, as if bearing the essence [of honey] in its own flowers out of passionate attachment to the honey-sweet voices of beautiful women humming with bees drunk on honey. The <s>kaṅkeli</s> (Aśoka) cluster, dark with swarms of bees falling intermittently upon it, like a half-extinguished funeral pyre of the god of love, bore the burning torment of wayfarers. The rows of blossoming buds, mottled with swarms of bees, shone like strings of sapphires and pearls adorning the beauty of spring. The <s>nāgakesara</s> (ironwood) flower appeared like a discus of the flower-armed god (<s>Kāmadeva</s>) for churning the hearts of women in separation. The <s>pāṭalī</s> (trumpet-flower) blossom appeared as the winnowing-fan of the <s>makara</s>-bannered god for snatching away the hearts of wayfarers.

children.text: tatra kecit kalāṅkurā iva vijitanagaramaṇḍanāḥ, apare pāṇḍavā iva divyacakṣuḥkṛṣṇāguruparimilitāḥ, anye śaraddivasā iva dūrapravṛddhāśāḥ, itare py āhartum udyatā iva svabalārthinaḥ, kecid vyādhā iva śakunaśrāvakāḥ, kecid ākheṭina iva rūpānusārapravṛttāḥ, kecij jaiminimataśrāviṇa iva tathāgata[mata]dhvaṃsinaḥ, kecit khañjanā iva sāṃvatsaraphaladarśinaḥ, kecit sumeruparisarā iva kārtasvaramayāḥ, kecit kumudākarā iva bhāsvaddarśananimīlitāḥ, kecid dhārtarāṣṭrā iva viśvarūpāvalokanajanitendrajālodbhūtapratyayāḥ, kecid ātmanivāraṇabuddhyā balavanto 'pi suvāhāḥ, kecit pāṇigrahaṇārthino 'py asukaraṃ manyamānāḥ, kecid adharībhūtā (a)pi sthirāḥ, kecit pāṇḍuputrā ivā[kṣahṛdayā]jñānahṛtakṣamāḥ, kecid bṛhatkathābandhino guṇāḍhyāḥ, kecit tiryaggatayo gandhavāhāḥ, kecit kauravasainikā iva droṇāśāsūcakāḥ, kecit kumudākarā ivāsoḍhabhāsaḥ kṣaṇam evaṃ sthitā rājaputrāḥ | sā ca kṣaṇenaikaikaśaḥ samavalokya kumārikā ta(s)māt karṇīrathād avatatāra |
children.translated_text: There, some princes were like buds of art, surpassing the ornaments of the city; others, like the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>, were surrounded by divine vision, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, and <s>aguru</s> incense; some were like autumn days with far-extended hopes; others were eager to seize [the bride], seeking their own power; some were like hunters attending to omens from birds; some were like huntsmen, proceeding in pursuit of beauty; some, like hearers of <s>Jaimini's</s> doctrine, were destroyers of the <s>Tathāgata's</s> (<s>Buddha's</s>) teaching; some were like wagtails, observing the astrological fruits; some were like the vicinity of <s>Sumeru</s>, made of gold; some were like groves of night-lilies, closed at the sight of the radiant [sun/bride]; some, like the sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, had convictions born of the illusion produced by beholding the universal form; some, though powerful, were easy to bear, with the thought of restraining themselves; some, though desirous of taking her hand, considered it impossible; some, though humbled, remained steadfast; some, like the sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, had their patience stolen by ignorance of the dice [of fate]; some, like the authors of the <s>Bṛhatkathā</s>, were rich in virtues (<s>Guṇāḍhya</s>); some moved sideways like wind-carriers (snakes); some, like <s>Kaurava</s> soldiers, indicated the hope of [reaching] <s>Droṇa</s>; some, like groves of night-lilies, unable to bear the radiance, stood thus for but a moment. And the maiden, having surveyed each one in an instant, descended from that <s>karṇīratha</s> (ear-chariot/balcony).

children.text: atha sā tasyām eva rātrau svapne vālinam ivāṅgadopaśobhitaṃ, kuhūmukham iva hārikaṇṭhaṃ, kanakamṛgam iva rāmākarṣaṇanipuṇaṃ, jayantam iva vacanāmṛtānanditavṛddhaśravasaṃ, kṛṣṇam iva kaṃ saharṣaṃ na kurvantaṃ, mahāmegham iva vilasatkarakaṃ, [samudram iva] mahāsattvaṃ, mālinyā kabarikayā, tuṅgabhadrayā nāsikayā, śoṇenādhareṇa, narmadayā vācā, godayā bhujayā svarvāhinyā kīrtyā ca puṇyamayam iva, ādikandaṃ śṛṅgārapādapasya, rohaṇagiriṃ sakalaguṇaratnasamūhasya, prabhavaśailaṃ sundarakathānadīnāṃ, surabhimāsaṃ vaidagdhyasahakārasya, ādarśatalaṃ saujanyamukhasya, ādikandaṃ vidyālatānāṃ, svayaṃvarapatiṃ sarasvatyāḥ, spardhāgṛhaṃ kīrtilakṣmyoḥ, ādigṛhaṃ śīlasaṃpadāṃ, kośam iva mahāsaundaryasya tribhuvanalobhanīyākṛtiṃ yuvānaṃ dadarśa |
children.translated_text: Then, on that very night, in a dream, she beheld a young man — beautified by armlets like <s>Vālin</s>; with a charming throat like the face of the new-moon night (<s>kuhū</s>); skilled in attracting beautiful women like the golden deer [attracted <s>Sītā</s>]; like <s>Jayanta</s>, whose old father <s>Vṛddhaśravas</s> was delighted by his nectarine words; like <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who made everyone joyful; like a great cloud with gleaming hailstones; [like the ocean,] of great courage; as if made holy — by the <s>Mālinī</s> river in his braid-like [locks], by the <s>Tuṅgabhadrā</s> in his nose, by the <s>Śoṇa</s> in his lower lip, by the <s>Narmadā</s> in his speech, by the <s>Godāvarī</s> in his arm, by the <s>Svarvāhinī</s> (Ganges) in his fame; the original root of the tree of <s>Śṛṅgāra</s> (love); the <s>Rohaṇa</s> mountain for the entire collection of quality-gems; the source-mountain of the rivers of beautiful tales; the spring month of the mango tree of elegance; the mirror-surface for the face of courtesy; the original root of the creepers of learning; the self-chosen lord of <s>Sarasvatī</s>; the arena of rivalry between Fame and Fortune; the original abode of virtuous accomplishments; the treasury of supreme beauty — of a form captivating to all three worlds.

"sa Cintāmaṇināmno rājñas tanayaḥ Kandarpaketur nāmeti" sā svapna eva nāmādikam aśrauṣīt | anantaraṃ "aho prajāpate rūpanirmāṇakauśalam idaṃ, manye svasyaiva naipuṇyasya saundaryadarśanotsukamanasā kamalabhuvā jagattrayasamavāye rūpaparamāṇūn ādādya viracito 'yam anyathā katham ayam asya kāntiviśeṣa" iti, "vṛthaiva damayantī nalasya kṛte vana[vāsa]vaiśasam avāpa, mudhaivendumatī mahiṣy apy ajānurāgiṇī babhūva, aphalam iva duṣyantasya kṛte śakuntalāpi durvāsasaḥ śāpam anubabhūva, nirarthakam iva madanamañjukā naravāhanadattaṃ cakame, niṣkāraṇam evorugarimanirjitarambhā[rambhā] nalakūbaram acīkamata, viphalam eva dhūmorṇā svayaṃvarārthagatadevagrahagandharvasahasreṣu dharmarājam akāṅkṣateti" bahudhiyā cintayantī virahamurmuramadhyam ārūḍheva vāḍavāgniśikhā[kavaliteva], kālāgnirudrapāvakagrasteva, pātālaguhāpraviṣṭeva, [śūnyakaraṇa]grāmālikhitam iva, utkīrṇam iva, nigalitam iva, vajralepaghaṭitam iva, astipañjarapraviṣṭam iva, marmāntarāsthitam iva, [majjārasaśabalitam iva], prāṇaparītam iva, antarātmānam adhiṣṭhitam iva, rudhirāśayadravībhūtam iva, palalasaṃvibhaktam iva Kandarpaketuṃ manyamānā, unmatteva, badhireva, mūkeva, śūnyeva, nirastakaraṇagrāmeva, mūrcchāgṛhīteva, grahagrasteva, yauvanasāgarataraṅgaparamparāparigateva, rāgarajjubhir apavāriteva, kandarpakusumabāṇaiḥ kīliteva, śṛṅgāraviṣaghūrṇiteva, rūpaparibhāvanaśalyakhilliteva, malayānilāhatajīviteva "priyasakhy Anaṅgalekhe vitara[me] hṛdaye pāṇipādaṃ duḥsaho virahasantāpaḥ, mugdhe Madanamañjari siñca candanodakena, sarale Vasantasene saṃvṛṇu keśakalāpapāśam, tarale Lavaṅgavati vikira ketakadhūliṃ, Mālini alaṃ śaivaladalena, capale Citralekhe likha citre cittacoraṃ janaṃ, bhāmini Vilāsavati vikṣipa muktācūrṇanikaram, rāgiṇi Rāgalekhe sthagaya nalinīdalasamūhena payodharabharam, sukānte Kāntimati mandaṃ mandam apanaya bāṣpabindūn, yū(thi)kālaṅkṛte Yū(thi)ke sañcāraya nalinīdalārdravātān, ehi bhagavati nidre anugṛhāṇa mām, dhig indriyair aparaiḥ, kim iti locanamayāni mamāṅgāni vidhinā na kṛtāni,
bhagavan kusumāyudha tavāyam añjalir anucaro, bhava bhāvavati tādṛśe jane, [malayānila] suratotkaṇṭhadīkṣāguro vaha yatheccham" iti bahuvidhaṃ bhāṣamāṇā Vāsavadattā sakhījanena samaṃ mumūrccha |
children.translated_text: She heard in that very dream [his] name and other details: 'He is the son of the king named <s>Cintāmaṇi</s>, called <s>Kandarpaketu</s>.' Thereupon [she thought]: 'Alas, what skill <s>Prajāpati</s> (the Creator) has in fashioning beauty! I think this one was fashioned by the Lotus-born (<s>Brahmā</s>), whose mind was eager to see the beauty of his own skill, having gathered the atoms of beauty from the assembly of the three worlds — for how else could this extraordinary radiance of his exist?' And [she thought]: 'In vain did <s>Damayantī</s> suffer the torment of forest-dwelling for <s>Nala's</s> sake; in vain did <s>Indumatī</s>, though a queen, become passionately devoted to her knees alone [in grief]; fruitlessly did <s>Śakuntalā</s> endure the curse of <s>Durvāsas</s> for <s>Duṣyanta's</s> sake; to no purpose did <s>Madanamañjukā</s> desire <s>Naravāhanadatta</s>; without reason did [<s>Rambhā</s>], whose pride was conquered by [<s>Nalakūbara's</s>] massive thighs, desire <s>Nalakūbara</s>; in vain did <s>Dhūmorṇā</s>, when thousands of gods, <s>Grahas</s>, and <s>Gandharvas</s> came to her <s>svayaṃvara</s>, long for <s>Dharmarāja</s> (<s>Yama</s>) alone.' Thinking thus in many ways, <s>Vāsavadattā</s>, as if mounted upon the churning of the waves of separation, as if swallowed by the flame of the submarine fire, as if consumed by the fire of the <s>Kālāgni Rudra</s>, as if fallen into the cave of the netherworld, as if [his image were] engraved upon the canvas of her empty senses, as if carved [upon her heart], as if poured into it, as if cemented there with diamond-paste, as if entered into her skeletal frame, as if lodged between her vital joints, as if mixed with the marrow-essence, as if encompassed by her very breath, as if seated within her inner self, as if dissolved in the reservoir of her blood, as if distributed through her flesh — considering <s>Kandarpaketu</s> thus [present in every fiber of her being], like one mad, like one deaf, like one mute, like one vacant, like one whose entire sense-faculty was cast away, as if seized by a swoon, as if possessed by a planet, as if engulfed by wave upon wave of the ocean of youth, as if bound by the ropes of passion, as if transfixed by <s>Kāmadeva's</s> flower-arrows, as if whirling from the poison of love, as if pierced by the thorn of beauty's overwhelming power, as if her life was struck by the <s>Malaya</s> breeze — she cried out: 'Dear friend <s>Anaṅgalekhā</s>, place your hand upon my heart — the burning of separation is unbearable! Sweet <s>Madanamañjarī</s>, sprinkle me with sandalwood-water! Honest <s>Vasantasenā</s>, cover me with the net of tresses! Restless <s>Lavaṅgavatī</s>, scatter <s>ketaka</s> (screwpine) pollen! O <s>Mālinī</s>, enough with the water-moss fronds! Fickle <s>Citralekhā</s>, paint in a picture that heart-thief! Passionate <s>Vilāsavatī</s>, scatter heaps of pearl-powder! Amorous <s>Rāgalekhā</s>, cover the weight of my breasts with lotus leaves! Lovely <s>Kāntimatī</s>, slowly, slowly wipe away my tear-drops! O <s>Yūthikā</s>, adorned with jasmines, fan me with breezes from moist lotus-leaves! Come, blessed Sleep, grace me! A curse upon these other senses — why did the Creator not make all my limbs consist of eyes alone? O blessed god of the flower-weapon (<s>Kāma</s>), here is my salutation — be my follower! Be disposed toward such a person! O <s>Malaya</s> breeze, guru of the consecration of longing for love, blow as you wish!' Speaking thus in many ways, <s>Vāsavadattā</s> fainted along with her company of friends.

children.text: anantaraṃ parijanaprayatnocchvāsitajīvitā ca, kṣanam atiśiśiraghanasārarajonimnagākūlapuline, kṣanam atituhinajaḍamalayarajasaḥ saritparisare, kṣaṇam aravindakānanaparivāritasarastaṭaviṭapacchāyāsu, kṣaṇam anilollāsitadaleṣu kadalīkānaneṣu, kṣaṇaṃ kusumaśayyāsu, kṣaṇaṃ nalinīdalasrastareṣu, kṣaṇaṃ tuṣārasaṃghātaśiśiritaśilātaleṣu parijanena nīyamānā, pralayakāloditadvādaśaravikiraṇakalāpatīvravirahāgnidahyamānā satī, atikṛśāṃ viprāṇām iva tanuṃ bibhratī, pracaladamandamandarāndolitaduḥkhasindhutaralatarataraṅgacchaṭādhavalahāsacchuritādharapallavaṃ tanmukhāravindaṃ, dvijakulam iva śrutipraṇayi tadīkṣaṇayugalaṃ, sahajasurabhimukhaparimalāmodam āghrātukāmā sudūranirgatanāsāvaṃśalakṣmīḥ, kalaṅkamuktendukalākomalā, pīyūṣaphenapaṭalapāṇdurāsyadvijapaṅktiḥ, tadadṛṣṭacaram anaṅgam atiśayānaṃ rūpaṃ, dhanyāni tāni [sthānāni] te ca janapadāḥ, puṇyanāmākṣarāṇi ca tāni sukṛtabhāñji yāny amunā pariṣkṛtānīti muhur muhuḥ paribhāvayantī, dikṣu vilikhitam iva, nabhasy utkīrṇam iva, locane pratibimbitam iva, citrapaṭalikhitam iva, puro darśitam ivetas tato vilokayantī vyatiṣṭhata |
children.translated_text: Thereafter, her life revived through the exertions of her attendants, she was led by her retinue — for a moment to the sandy banks of a river of exceedingly cool camphor dust, for a moment to the vicinity of a stream of chilly Malaya sandalwood dust, for a moment into the shade of trees on the banks of lakes surrounded by lotus groves, for a moment into plantain groves with leaves rustling in the breeze, for a moment onto flower-beds, for a moment onto beds of lotus-leaves, for a moment onto stone surfaces cooled by masses of dew — being burned by the fierce fire of separation, as intense as the rays of the twelve suns at the time of cosmic dissolution; bearing a body as emaciated as that of ascetic <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>; her lotus-face with its lip-sprouts sprinkled with the white laughter resembling the trembling wave-crests of the ocean of sorrow churned by the shaking of the trembling <s>Mandara</s> mountain; her pair of eyes devoted to hearing like a family of twice-born (<s>dvija</s>); the beauty of her nose-bridge extending far out as if desiring to smell the innate sweet fragrance of her face; soft as a moonbeam freed from its blemish; her row of teeth white as layers of nectar-foam on her face; [contemplating] that form surpassing even <s>Anaṅga</s> (the bodiless Love-god), invisible to direct sight — "Blessed are those places and those peoples, and blessed those syllables of meritorious names, which have been adorned by him" — contemplating thus again and again, as if inscribed in the directions, as if engraved in the sky, as if reflected in her eye, as if painted on a canvas, as if displayed before her — gazing here and there, she stood.

children.text: atha tasyāḥ sārikā Tamālikā nāma tatsakhībhiḥ sahālocya Kandarpaketor bhāvam ākalayituṃ [pra]sthitā | āgatā ca mayaiva sārdham atraiva taror adhas tiṣṭhatīty" uktvā virarāma |
children.translated_text: Then her <s>sārikā</s> (myna bird) named <s>Tamālikā</s>, having consulted with her friends, set out to ascertain the feelings of <s>Kandarpaketu</s>. "And she has come with me and is standing right here beneath this tree" — having said this, she fell silent.

children.text: atha saharṣam utthāya Makarando viditavṛttāntāṃ Tamālikām akarot | sā ca kṛtapraṇāmā Kandarpaketave patrikām upānayata | atha sa tāṃ svayam avācayata |
children.translated_text: Then, rising joyfully, <s>Makaranda</s> acquainted <s>Tamālikā</s> with the events. And she, having bowed, presented a letter to <s>Kandarpaketu</s>. Then he himself read it aloud:

children.text: pratyakṣadṛṣṭabhāvāpy asthirahṛdayā hi kāminī bhavati /
