children.text: tac chrutvā Kandarpaketur amṛtārṇavamagnam iva sarvānandānām upari vartamāno mandaṃ mandam utthāya prasāritabāhuyugalas tām āliliṅga | atha tayaiva sārdhaṃ samāsīnaḥ "kiṃ vadati, kiṃ karoti, katham āsta" ityādi sakalaṃ vṛttāntaṃ pṛcchaṃs tāṃ niśāṃ dinam apy ativāhya cacāla Kandarpaketuḥ | atrāntare bhagavān api marīcimālī enaṃ vṛttāntam iva kathayituṃ madhyamaṃ lokam avātarat |
children.translated_text: Hearing that, <s>Kandarpaketu</s>, as if immersed in an ocean of nectar, rising above all joys, slowly rising with arms outstretched, embraced her. Then, seated together with her, asking about all the details — "What does she say? What does she do? How is she?" — and so on, having passed that night and the day as well, <s>Kandarpaketu</s> set forth. Meanwhile, the blessed Sun (<s>Marīcimālī</s>), as if to narrate these events, descended to the middle world.

children.text: atha vāsaratāmracūḍacakrākāraḥ cakravākacakrasaṅkramitasantāpatayeva mandimānam udvahanmandārastabakasundaraḥ, sindūrāhatasuragajakumbhavibhramaṃ bibhrāṇaḥ, tāṇḍavacaṇḍavegocchalitadhūrjaṭijaṭājūṭakūṭabandhabandhuravikaṭavāsukibhogamaṇitāṭaṅkasaṅkāśanābhimaṇḍalaḥ, sandhyāsandhinīsarasayāvakapaṭacāruḥ, vāruṇivāravilāsinīmaṇikuntalakāntiḥ, dinakaracchinnavāsarakabandhacakrākaraḥ, madhupūrṇakapāla iva kālakapālinaḥ, amlānakusumastabaka iva śriyaḥ, gaganāśokatarustabakaḥ [iva], kanakadarpaṇa iva pratīcīvilāsinyāḥ, balabhadra iva vāruṇīsaṅgataḥ sarāgaś ca, durvidha iva parityaktavasuḥ saviṣādaś ca, śā(kya) iva raktāṃśukadharaḥ, saṃjñopeto bhagavān caramārṇavapayasi taralataraṅgavegocchalitavidrumavikaṭākṛtir mamajja |
children.translated_text: Then the day-crested-rooster-wheeled [sun], beautiful as a cluster of <s>mandāra</s> flowers, bearing a dimness as if the heat had been transmitted to the <s>cakravāka</s> circle, displaying the appearance of a temple-globe of a divine elephant struck with vermillion, with a navel-disc resembling the jeweled earring on the terrible <s>Vāsuki</s> serpent's hood coiling atop the matted locks of the fierce-rushing <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s> (<s>Śiva</s>) in the wild fury of his <s>tāṇḍava</s> dance, beautiful with the lovely lac-dyed garment of the twilight at the junction, with the jewel-lustre of the tresses of the beauty of the western quarter (<s>Vāruṇī</s>), wheeled by the day-severed-day-headless-corpse-circle, like a skull filled with wine of <s>Kālakapālī</s> (Time, the skull-bearer), like an unfading cluster of blossoms of <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune), like a cluster of blossoms of the heavenly <s>aśoka</s> tree, like a golden mirror of the western beauty, like <s>Balabhadra</s> united with <s>Vāruṇī</s> (wine) and passionate, like a vile one who has abandoned wealth and is sorrowful, like a Buddhist monk clad in red garments, endowed with consciousness — the blessed sun sank into the waters of the western ocean, his form made terrible by coral-like shapes tossed by the heaving wave-crests.

children.text: krameṇa ca rajoluṭhitotthitakulāyārthikalahavikalakalaviṅkakulakalakalavācālitaśikhareṣu śikhariṣu, vasatisākāṅkṣeṣu dhvāṅkṣeṣu, anavaratadahyamānakālāgurudhūpaparimalodgāreṣu vāsāgāreṣu, dūrvānvitataṭinībaddhagoṣṭhīkavidagdhajanaprastūyamānakathāśravaṇotsukaśiśujanakalakalanivāraṇakupitaśraddheṣu vṛddheṣu, ālolikātaralarasanābhiḥ kathitakathābhir jaratībhir atilaghukaratāḍanajanitasukhe, śiśayiṣamāṇaśiśujane, viracitakandarpamudrāsu kṣudrāsu, kāmukajanānubaddhyamānadāsījanavividhāślīlavacanaśrutivirasīkṛtasandhyāvandanopaviṣṭeṣu śiṣṭeṣu, romanthamantharakuraṅgakuṭumbakādhyāsyamānamradiṣṭhagauṣṭhīnapṛṣṭhāsv araṇyasthalīṣu, nidrāvinidrāṇadroṇakulakalitakulāyeṣv ārāmataruṣu, nirjigamiṣati jarattarukoṭarakuṭīrakuṭumbini kauśikakule, timiratarjananirgatāsu dahanapraviṣṭadinakarakiraṇāsv iva sphurantīṣu dīpalekhāsu, mukharitadhanuṣi varṣati śaranikaram anavaratam aśeṣasaṃsāraśemuṣīmuṣi makaradhvaje, suratārambhākalpaśobhini, śambhalībhāṣitabhāji bhajati bhuṣāṃ bhujiṣyajane, sairandhrībadhyamānaraśanājālajalpākajaghanāsu janīṣu, viśrāntakathānubandhatayā pravartamānakathakajanagṛhagamanatvareṣu catvareṣu, samāvāsitakukk(u)ṭeṣu niṣkuṭeṣu, kṛtayaṣṭisamārohaṇeṣu barhiṇeṣu, vihitasandhyāsamayavyavasthiteṣu gṛhasthaleṣu, saṅkocodañcaduccakesarakoṭisaṅkaṭakuśeśayakośakoṭarakuṭhīraśāyini ṣaṭcaraṇacakre, athānena pravartatā [vartmanā] bhagavatā bhānunā [ā]gantavyam iti sarvapaṭṭamayair vasanair iva maṇikuṭṭimābhir viracitavaruṇena, bhagavatā kālena kṛttasya divasamahiṣasya rudhi(ra)dhāreva, vidrumalatevāmbaramahārṇavasya, raktakamalinīva gaganataḍākasya, kāñcanasetur iva kandarpasya, mañjiṣṭhārāgāruṇapatākeva gaganaharmyatalasya, lakṣmīr iva svayaṃvaragṛhītapītāmbarasya, bhikṣukīva tārānurāgaraktā, raktāmbaradhāriṇīva bhagavatī sandhyā samadṛśyata |
children.translated_text: And gradually — when on the mountain-peaks whose summits were made noisy by the quarrelsome clamor of flocks of sparrows rising from the dust to seek their nests; when the crows were eager for their roosts; when the pleasure-houses were fragrant with the exhalation of the scent of constantly burning black aloe incense; when the old men, their faith angered by the effort of silencing the clamor of children eager to hear the stories being recited by clever people gathered in assemblies on the river-banks bordered with <s>dūrvā</s> grass, took pleasure in the gentle hand-clapping [to quiet them]; when the children were about to sleep; when the wanton women had assumed the seal-gestures of <s>Kandarpa</s> (Love); when the virtuous men, seated for evening worship, were made weary in their hearing by the various improper words of the servant-women being followed by amorous men; when the wilderness grounds had their backs occupied by herds of deer families slowly chewing their cud on the tops of lowered threshing-floor platforms; when the garden trees had their nests adorned by the drowsy flocks of <s>Droṇa</s> birds subdued by sleep; when the owl families, dwelling in the hollows of old tree-trunks, wished to go forth; when the lamp-flames were flashing as if the fire-entered daylight-rays were emerging to terrify the darkness; when the flower-arrowed Love-god, his bow-string resonant, was showering an unceasing volley of arrows, robbing the entire world of its composure; when the love-sport was beginning to shine with beauty; when the maidservants were donning their ornaments while speaking the language of <s>Śambhalī</s> (a barbarian tongue); when the women had their hips bound with girdle-nets being tied by their <s>sairandhrī</s> (chambermaid), the jingling of which was like babbling; when the public squares were bustling with people hurrying to the houses of storytellers as the narrative-threads of their tales resumed; when the peacocks had mounted their staffs (perches) in the garden-enclosures where roosters were settled; when the households were arranged in their proper evening-time order; when the swarms of bees were sleeping in the hollow cells of the water-lily buds whose pointed petal-tips were contracting and rising upward — then twilight (<s>sandhyā</s>) was seen: prepared by <s>Varuṇa</s> with pavements all of silk as if with garments for the arrival of the blessed sun on this advancing path; like a stream of blood of the great buffalo of Day slain by blessed <s>Kāla</s> (Time); like a coral vine of the great ocean of the sky; like a red lotus-pool in the lake of the heavens; like a golden bridge of <s>Kandarpa</s> (Love); like a vermillion-red banner on the rooftop palace of the sky; like <s>Lakṣmī</s> who had herself chosen the yellow-robed one (<s>Viṣṇu</s>); like a mendicant nun dyed red with affection for the stars; like a wearer of red garments — the blessed <s>Sandhyā</s> (Twilight) was seen.

children.text: kṣaṇena ca kṣaṇadārāgaracanācaturāsu sandhyāśiṣyāsv iva veśyāsu tulādhāraśūnyāyāṃ paṇyavīthyām iva divi, ghanaghanāyamānadalapuṭāsu puṭakinīṣu, timirapratihasteṣv iva tata itaḥ (pa)ribhramatsu kamalasarasi madhukareṣu, vikalakurarīrutacchalena ravivirahavidhurāsu vilapantīṣv iva sarojinīṣu, kamalinīsandhyārāgarajyamānasalilasthitāsu pativināśahṛtpīḍyā dahanapraviṣṭāsv iva kamalinīṣu, gaṇaka iva nakṣatrasūcake pradoṣasamaye, harakaṇṭhakāṇḍakālimasanābhi, daityabalam iva prakaṭatārakaṃ, bhāratasamaram iva vardhamānolūkakalakalaṃ, dhṛṣṭadyumnavīryam iva kuṇṭhitadroṇaprabhāvaṃ, nandanavanam iva saṃcaratkauśikaṃ, kṛṣṇavartmevākhilakāṣṭhāpahārakaṃ, sagarbham iva ghanatarapāṣāṇakarkaśāsu giritaṭīṣu, sacakṣur iva suptasiṃhanayanacchavicchaṭākapilikeṣu sānuṣu, sajīvam iva tamomaṇibhiḥ, saṃvardhitam ivāgnihotradhūmalekhābhir māsalitam iva kāminīkeśapāśasaṃskāradhūpapaṭalaiḥ, uddīpitam iva ghanataralīnamadhukarapaṭalamecakitapecakikapolataladānadhārāśīkaraiḥ, puñjīkṛtam iva vitatamālatamālakānanacchāyāsu, līyamānam iva kajjalarasaśyāmabhogibhogeṣu, prāvaraṇam iva rajanīpāṃsulāyāḥ, palitauṣadham iva vṛddhavārayoṣitām, apatyam iva rajanyāḥ, suhṛd iva kalikālasya, mitram iva durjanahṛdayānāṃ, bauddhasiddhāntam iva pratyakṣadravyam apahnuvānaṃ timiram ajṛmbhata |
children.translated_text: And in a moment — when in the courtesans, skilled in the artful preparations of the night as if they were students of <s>Sandhyā</s> (Twilight); when in the heavens like a market-street empty of its balance-scales; when in the buds whose leaf-folds were densely closing; when in the bees wandering here and there as if warding off the darkness with their hands; when in the lotus-pools that seemed to be lamenting the separation from the sun under the pretext of the pitiful cries of <s>kurarī</s> (osprey) birds; when in the lotuses standing in water reddened by the twilight-glow of the lotus-pool as if they had entered the fire from the heart-pain of losing their lord (the sun); when at the evening hour like an astrologer indicating the stars (<s>nakṣatras</s>) — the darkness, with a navel dark as the blackness on <s>Hara's</s> (<s>Śiva's</s>) throat; like the army of the <s>Daityas</s> (demons) with prominent stars (<s>Tāraka</s>); like the great <s>Bhārata</s> war with the increasing clamor of owls; like the valor of <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s>, blunting the power of <s>Droṇa</s> (darkness/the teacher); like the <s>Nandana</s> garden with <s>Kauśika</s> (owls/<s>Indra</s>) wandering about; like a fire-path, carrying off all [fuel from every] direction; seeming pregnant, on the rugged rocky mountain-slopes; seeming to have eyes, on the peaks with the tawny gleam of sleeping lions' eyes; seeming alive, through the darkness-gems (<s>tamomaṇi</s>); seeming augmented by the smoke-streaks of the <s>agnihotra</s> (fire-sacrifice); seeming smeared by the incense-clouds of the hair-dressing perfume of amorous women; seeming kindled by the dark drops of ichor-spray from the cheek-lobes of bees concealed within the dense clouds; seeming gathered together in the shades of the extended <s>tamāla</s> tree groves; seeming to hide in the dark collyrium-black coils of serpents; like the mantle of Night, dust-covered; like the gray-hair remedy of aged courtesans; like the offspring of Night; like the companion of the <s>Kali</s> age; like the friend of wicked hearts; like a Buddhist doctrine, denying perceptible substance — the darkness expanded.

children.text: muditam ivātimattamātaṅgamaṇḍalamanoharagaṇḍamaṇḍale, phalitam ivātisāndrabahalacchadavitatatamālakānane, sphuritam ivātikāntakāntājanaghanatarakeśasaṃhatau, malitam ivendranīlamaṇiraśmibhiḥ, atiśayamāṃsalaṃ tamo 'vaṭataṭāṭavīṣu, sāṭopam atisphuṭapāṭavotkaṭaprakaṭaviśaṅkaṭaikaviṭapotkaṭavinaṭitaṣaṭpadāliṣu, ghanataraghoraṃ, atighasmaraviṣadharabhogabhāsuraṃ, madabharamattadantidantadyutitarjanajarjaram | tato niśākarārambhasamaya iva saṃkucatkuvalayavyājaviracitāñjalipuṭe namati tamitimire, kṣaṇena ca sandhyātāṇḍavaḍambarocchalitamahānaṭajaṭājūṭakūṭakuṭilavivaravartijahanukanyāvāridhārābindava iva vikīrṇāḥ, durdharadharaṇibhārabhugnabhīmadiṅmātaṅgamaṇḍalāmuktaśīkaracchaṭā ivātitatāḥ, atidavīyonabhastalabhramaṇakhinnadinakaraturagavisaravāntaphenastabakā iva [vistīrṇāḥ], gaganamahāsaraḥkumudakānanasandehadāyinaḥ, viśvaṃ gaṇayatovidhātuḥ śaśikamaṭhinīkhaṇḍena tamomaṣīśyāme 'jina iva viyati saṃsārasyātiśūnyatvāc chūnyabindava iva vitatāḥ, jagattrayavijayanirgatasya kusumaketo ratikaratalavikīrṇalājā iva, gulikāstragulikā iva puṣpadhanuṣaḥ, viyadamburāśiphenastabakā iva, rativiracitā gaganāṅgaṇe ātarpaṇapañcāṅgulaya iva, vyomalakṣmīhāramuktānikarā iva, candracitācakrād vātyāvegavyastāḥ kāmakīkasakhaṇḍā iva, timirodgamadhūmadhūmalasandhyāmalāhitagaganamahāsthalīmahākaṭāhabhṛjjyamānasphuṭitalājānukārās tārā vyarājanta | tābhiś ca śvitrīva viyad aśobhata |
children.translated_text: As if rejoicing on the charming cheeks of circles of deeply intoxicated elephants, as if fruiting in forests of <s>tamāla</s> trees spreading dense thick leaves, as if throbbing in the very dense mass of hair of the most beautiful women, as if enveloped by the rays of sapphire gems — exceedingly dense darkness filled the forests on the banks of chasms, proudly filling the rows of trees where bees sported on prominent single branches with conspicuous dexterity, denser and more terrible, shining with the coils of all-devouring serpents, shattered by the threatening gleam of tusks of elephants heavy with rut. Then, as the darkness bowed low with folded palms fashioned under the pretext of closing water-lilies, as at the time of the moon's rising, in a moment the stars shone forth — like scattered drops from the water-streams of <s>Gaṅgā</s> flowing through the winding hollows of the matted hair-crest of the great dancer (<s>Śiva</s>) whose spectacle leapt forth in the dance of twilight; like spray released from the fearsome circle of direction-elephants bent under the unbearable weight of the earth; like clusters of foam vomited by the horses of the sun, weary from traversing the far-distant sky; creating the doubt of being a garden of <s>kumuda</s> (night-lotuses) in the great lake of the sky; like zero-dots spread on a deer-skin of sky blackened with the ink of darkness, written with the moon-pen fragment by the Creator counting the universe; like parched grains scattered from the palm of <s>Rati</s> in the marriage procession of the flower-bannered one (<s>Kāmadeva</s>) setting forth to conquer the three worlds; like pellet-missiles of the flower-bow; like clusters of foam from the ocean of the sky; like the five-fingered <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libation) made by <s>Rati</s> on the courtyard of the sky; like heaps of pearls from the necklace of the goddess of the sky; like fragments of <s>Kāma</s>'s garment scattered by a whirlwind from the funeral pyre of the moon; imitating parched grains being fried in the great cauldron-like plain of the sky, made murky by the smoky-lazy twilight from the rising of darkness — the stars shone brilliantly. And with them, the sky appeared as if afflicted with vitiligo.

children.text: tato dīrghocchvāsaracanākuśalaṃ saśleṣabahughaṭanāpaṭu satkaviviracanam iva, cakravākamithunam atīvākhidyata | kamalinīsañcaraṇalagnamakarandabindulavamadhukaramālāśabalagātraṃ, kālapāśeneva mūrtarāmaśāpenākṛṣyamāṇaṃ cakravākamithunam vijaghaṭe | ravivirahavidhurāyāḥ kamalinyā hṛdayam iva dvidhā papāṭa cakravākamithunam | āgamiṣyato himakaradayitasya pārśve saṃcarantī kumudinyā bhramaramālā dūtīvālakṣyata | tārakāvyājād astaṅgatasya divākarasya śokād iva kakubho vyarudan | bhāsvato nijadayitasya virahād abhinavakiñjalkarāśivyājena murmura iva nalinīkośahṛdaye jajvāla | raviraśmibhasmitanabhovanamaṣīrāśir iva, śrutivacanam iva kṣatadigambaradarśanaṃ, kṛṣṇarūpam api tiraskṛtaviśvarūpabhāvaṃ, sadyodrāvitarājatapaṭṭasamudrapravāha iva śārvaram andhakāram ajṛmbhata |
children.translated_text: Then, like the composition of a good poet, skilled in fashioning long sighs (<s>dīrghocchvāsa</s>/extended verses) and adept at extensive arrangement with double-meanings (<s>śleṣa</s>), the <s>cakravāka</s> (ruddy sheldrake) pair was exceedingly distressed. Its bodies speckled with strings of bees clinging to drops of nectar from roaming among lotuses, as if being dragged by the noose of Time, as if by the embodied curse of <s>Rāma</s>, the <s>cakravāka</s> pair was separated. Like the heart of the lotus-pond distressed by separation from the sun, the <s>cakravāka</s> pair split in two. The string of bees roaming near the <s>kumudinī</s> (night-lotus pond), beloved of the approaching moon, appeared like a female messenger. Under the pretext of stars, the quarters wept as if from grief for the departed sun. As if from separation from its beloved, the radiant one, a murmuring fire blazed in the heart of the lotus-bud under the pretext of fresh filaments. Like a heap of ink from the sky-forest reduced to ashes by the sun's rays, like a Vedic statement condemning the sight of the naked (sky-clad) quarters, though having the form of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> yet concealing the universal form, like a stream of suddenly melted silver — the darkness of night expanded.

children.text: kṣaṇena ca kṣaṇadārājakanyākanduka iva, kandarpakanakadarpaṇa iva, udayagiribālamandārastabakākṛtiḥ, prācīlalāṭakusumacakrākāraḥ, kuṇḍalam iva nabhaśriyaḥ, divyavadhūprasādhikāhastasrastālaktapaṭa iva, gaganasaudhakanakakumbha iva, prasthānakalaśa iva tribhuvanavijayanirgatasya makaraketoḥ, kandarpakārtasvaratūṇamukhacakrakāntitaskaraḥ, prākśailaśikharāgraprarūḍhajavātarukusumacchaviḥ, acchakuṅkumapiṇḍapūrṇasthita[pātra] iva niśāvilāsinyāḥ kuṅkumāruṇaśveta[stana]kalaśa iva cākhaṇḍalāśāyāḥ, udayāruṇamaṇḍalo rajanīpatir abhyudayam āsasāda |
children.translated_text: And in a moment, like a ball for the princess of the king of the night, like a golden mirror of <s>Kandarpa</s> (Love), having the form of a cluster of young <s>mandāra</s> flowers on the rising mountain, round like a <s>tilaka</s> ornament on the forehead of the east, like an earring of the beauty of the sky, like a lac-dyed cloth slipped from the hand of a divine bride's attendant, like a golden finial atop a palace of the sky, like a departure-vessel for the crocodile-bannered one (<s>Kāmadeva</s>) setting out to conquer the three worlds, stealing the lustre of the mouth of <s>Kandarpa</s>'s golden quiver, with the hue of <s>javā</s> flowers growing on the peak of the eastern mountain, like a vessel filled with a ball of pure saffron, like the saffron-reddened white breast-pot of the coquettish Night and of <s>Indra</s>'s eastern quarter — the lord of the night, with a rising-reddened orb, attained his ascent.

children.text: tataḥ kāminīhṛdayasaṅkrāmita iva cakorāṅganānetrapuṭapāṭita iva raktakumudakośakīṭa iva kṣīṇatāṃ jagāma kṣaṇadākṛto rāgaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then the redness born of night faded — as if transferred to the hearts of lovers, as if split open by the eyes of <s>cakora</s> hens, as if being an insect in a red night-lotus bud.

children.text: anantaraṃ śarvarīvrajāṅganāniṣṭhyūtanavanītasvastika iva, kusumaketor mukhacchāyāmudrita iva, śvetātapatram iva makaraketoḥ, dantapālicakra iva viyanmahāseḥ, śvetacāmara iva madanamahārājasya, bālapulinam iva niśāyamunāyāḥ, sphuṭikaliṅgam iva gaganatāpasasya, aṇḍam iva kāloragasya, kambur iva nabhomahārṇavasya, caityam iva madanāridagdhasya makaraketoḥ, citācakram iva kalaṅkāṅgāraśabalaṃ saṅkalpajanmanaḥ, gaganagāmipuṇḍarīkam iva, ambaramahārṇavaphenapuñja iva, pāradapiṇḍa iva [kāladhātuvādinaḥ], rājatakalaśa iva dūrvāpravālaśabalaḥ, kandarparathacakracāruḥ, udayācalacūḍāmaṇiḥ, ambaramahāprāsādapārāvataḥ, airāvatakumbhasthalam iva, bhagnaśṛṅgapurāṇagomuṇḍa iva, tārakāśvetagodhūmaśālino nabhaḥkṣetrasya, pāṇḍurarājatapātram iva siddhāṅganāhastasrasto grahapatir ujjagāma | yaś ca puṇḍarīkaṃ locanamadhukarāṇāṃ, śayanīyasaikataṃ cittahaṃsānāṃ, sphaṭikavyajanaṃ virahavahnīnām |
children.translated_text: Then, like a <s>svastika</s> of fresh butter spat out by the cowherd-women of the night, as if stamped with the facial reflection of the flower-bannered one (<s>Kāmadeva</s>), like a white parasol of the crocodile-bannered one, like an ivory shield of the great army of the sky, like a white fly-whisk of King <s>Madana</s> (Love), like a fresh sandbank of the night-<s>Yamunā</s>, like a crystal <s>liṅga</s> of the sky-ascetic, like the egg of the serpent of Time, like a conch of the great ocean of the sky, like a memorial mound for the crocodile-bannered one burnt by the enemy of <s>Madana</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), like a funeral pyre-wheel speckled with charcoal-stains for one born from thought, like a sky-going white lotus, like a heap of foam from the great ocean of the sky, like a ball of mercury, like a silver pot speckled with <s>dūrvā</s> grass sprouts, beautiful as the wheel of <s>Kandarpa</s>'s chariot, the crest-jewel of the eastern mountain, the dove of the great palace of the sky, like the temple of <s>Airāvata</s> (<s>Indra</s>'s elephant), like an ancient bull's head with broken horns, like a pale silver vessel for the sky-field whose rice is the white wheat of stars — the lord of planets, as if slipped from the hands of <s>Siddhā</s> women, rose. He who is a white lotus for the bees of the eyes, a sandy bed for the swans of the mind, a crystal fan for the fires of separation.

children.text:

children.translated_text: Meanwhile there arose double-meaning, elaborate, and ambiguously shifting speeches of the go-between women (<s>dūtīs</s>) sent by groups of women going on trysts (<s>abhisārikās</s>) to their beloveds. Thus: "You do not truly perceive yourself reduced to a womanish state. Like a stone you are cruel. You are not even one among attractors, magnets, or solvents — you are merely a deceiver, O cheat! Not employed for the purpose of smelting, like a water-channel you vainly carry swift-flowing water. With sorrowful mind you think of the unattainable one. One whose conduct has the essence of courage stands content before an enemy host. He indeed is a hero who leads elephants away from the adversary through combat. Even one who holds a great collection of swords is truly a supreme arrow — he wins this great prize through battle. Deprived of passion, one is certainly not deprived of royal quality. Skilled, bright as a clear cloud, with clear self — able to protect majesty from the serpent of pride, O ornament of patience, your heroism is heroism in the mind, your truth is truth in speech. With daring, with that laughter, <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>), she who dwells in lotuses, is won. She, your mirror — with a mirror-like pure heart, with fingers surpassing lotus-shoots in grace — looks through the lattice-window gaps with trembling, with trembling, and without curses endures her sorrows. O lord of her life, for her life, who here does not resort to the blessed one? Let others remain in servitude — before them I alone worship; let friendship, let friendship prevail! Sincerely, essentially, why do you not extend some passion, some pride, to <s>Kandarpa</s>? Utterly, entirely, death stands certain! O purifier of the thoughts of rogues, O treasure of fame, the prize that cannot be seized, she who cannot be seized, with sidelong glances, with sidelong glances, her attendants have become your slaves from that face, from that moment. The face of women of lotus-form, of women of lotus-form, has been defiled by you. Having trusted, having trusted in your commitment, having entered into, having entered into musical harmony for many seasons, thin of body, thin from the arrow-pains of bodiless <s>Kandarpa</s>, among flowers, with arrow-wounds swiftly, with desire newly born, sluggish, sluggish, she wanders a moment and swoons. With lips sweet as passion, with lips sweet as honey, adorned with a streak of beauty-marks, with special marks, with a moon-face, clinging to your heart, tender of touch, tender of hand, with breasts bearing drops of sweat, with breasts like clouds, with a golden chest-plate, surpassing pure gold — O cruel in love, with rut-reddened eyes, O Love-filled one, she delighting, delighting you, merciless, intoxicating, desires you as her supreme lover, with a charming, charming breast-pot, with eyes stealing the beauty of a doe's, with a charming, charming gaze." Then, as if the world had entered the Milk Ocean, as if it had entered a crystal mansion, as if experiencing the bliss of dwelling on the White Island, the world rejoiced.

children.text: anantaraṃ kaṭakaikadeśaviracitaikāntanihitamuktāmakarandapadmarāgaśakalena Vāsavadattādarśanārtham āsthitena devatāgaṇeneva jātavalayena parigatam, anilollāsitābhir nabhastarumañjarībhir iva tarjayantībhir iva gaganapuraśriyaṃ patākābhir upaśobhamānaṃ, paṭṭāṅkaṇaprasṛtābhiḥ karpūracandanakuṅkumailāgandhodakarasaparimalavāhinībhir vāhinībhis taṭasphaṭikapaṭṭasukhaniṣaṇṇanidrāyamāṇājñātaprāsādapārāvatālibhiḥ prabhraśyattaṭaviṭapakusumastabakitasalilābhir anavaratamajjadunmadayuvatijanajaghanāsphālanocchvasitaśīkaranikarasnapitavedikābhiḥ, karpūrapūraviracitapulinatalaniṣaṇṇaninadānumīyamānarājahaṃsībhiḥ, vikacanīlotpalakānanadarśitākāṇḍacakravākatimiraśaṅkābhiḥ, yuvatībhir iva supayodharābhiḥ, sugrīvayuddhakalābhir iva kīlālasnapitakumbhakarṇābhiḥ, sāgarakūlabhūmibhir iva sundarīpādaparāgaśabalābhiḥ, navanṛpaticittavṛttibhir iva kulyāyamānakariṇībhiḥ, śikharagatamuktājālavyājena yuvatijanadarśanāgataṃ tārāgaṇam udvahadbhiḥ, kācakalaśākṛtim udvahantībhiḥ śikhisaṃhatibhir udbhāsitaiḥ prāsādair upaśobhitaṃ, kālāgarudhūpapaṭalair darśitākālajaladonnāham, kvacidgambhīramurajaravāhūtamandamandanartitanīlakaṇṭhaṃ, sāyaṃsamayam iva nipatitalokalocanaṃ, janakayajñasthānam iva dārotsukitarāmaṃ, mānuṣam ivābhinanditasurataṃ, nidhānam iva kautukasya, āvāsam iva śṛṅgārasya, kulagṛham iva vibhramasya, saṅketasthānam iva saundaryasya, Vāsavadattābhavanaṃ bhavanandanaprabhāvo dadarśa |
children.translated_text: Then he beheld <s>Vāsavadattā's</s> palace — surrounded, as if by a host of deities who had come to behold <s>Vāsavadattā</s>, by a bracelet-like ring formed of pearls, <s>makaranda</s> (nectar), and ruby fragments set in a secluded portion of the encampment; adorned with banners that, like blossoming sky-tree clusters stirred by the wind, seemed to threaten the beauty of the aerial city; [graced] with streams flowing from the silken courtyards, bearing the fragrance of camphor, sandalwood, saffron, cardamom, and perfumed water, upon whose crystal-slab banks palace pigeons sat comfortably dozing unaware, whose waters were streaked with flower-cluster blossoms falling from the bank-side branches, whose platforms were sprinkled by spray-showers raised from the hip-splashing of intoxicated young women constantly bathing; where royal geese could be inferred from their calls as sitting on sandbanks made of camphor-dust; where groves of blooming blue lotuses (<s>nīlotpala</s>) created the false fear of untimely darkness through [the appearance of] <s>cakravāka</s> birds; [the streams] well-breasted like young women; with <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>-sized [vessels] bathed in water like the battle-art of <s>Sugrīva</s>; variegated with the foot-powder of beauties like ocean-shore lands; like the mental states of a new king, with elephantesses flowing in channels — [the palace] with its peak-hung pearl-nets seemed to carry the star-hosts come to see the young women, radiant with peacock flocks bearing the form of crystal vases; displaying clouds of dark <s>agaru</s> (aloe-wood) incense that mimicked untimely rainclouds; where the deep rumble of drums somewhere invited peacocks to dance slowly — like the evening, captivating the eyes of all people; like the <s>yajña</s>-ground of <s>Janaka</s>, filling <s>Rāma</s> with longing; like human life, delighting in love (<s>surata</s>); a treasury of wonder; a dwelling of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic) sentiment; a family home of enchantment; a trysting place of beauty — he, the joy-bringer of his family, beheld <s>Vāsavadattā's</s> palace.

| Sañjīvanike vitara jīvajjīvakamithunāya maricapallavam | Pallavike pallavaya karpūradhūlibhiḥ kṛtrimaketakakānanam | Sahakāramañjari sañjanaya sahakārasaurabhaṃ vyajanavāteṣu | Madanalekhe lekhaya madanalekhaṃ malayānilasya | Makarike dehi mṛṇālāṅkuraṃ rājahaṃsaśāvakebhyaḥ | Vilāsavati vilāsaya mayūrakiśorakam | Tamālike [pari]malaya malayajarasena bhavanavāṭam | Kāñcanike vikira kastūridravaṃ kāñcanamaṇḍapikāyām | Pravālike secaya ghusṛṇarasena bālapravālakānanam" ity anyonyapraṇayapeśalāḥ pramadānām ālāpakathāḥ śṛṇvan Kandarpaketur Makarandena samaṃ vismayam akaron manasi "aho bhavanānām atiśāyi saundaryam | aho śṛṅgāraracanākauśalam | tathā hi tatkālalīlādalitamālavīdaśanakāṇtikomalakāntadantaghaṭito maṇḍapaḥ | asāv api karpūraśalākānirmitayantrapañjarasaṃyataḥ krīḍāśuka" ityādi paricintayan praviśya vyākaraṇeneva saraktapādena, bhāraten(ev)a suparvaṇā, rāmāyaṇeneva sundarakāṇḍacāruṇā jaṅghāyugalena virājamānāṃ, chandovicitir iva bhrājamānatanumadhyāṃ, nakṣatravidyām iva gaṇanīyahastaśravaṇāṃ, nyāyasthitim ivodyotakarasvarūpāṃ, bauddhasaṅgītim ivālaṅkāraprasādhitāṃ, upaniṣadam iva sānandātmakam udyotayantīṃ, dvijakulasthitim iva cārucaraṇāṃ, vindhyagiriśriyam iva sunitambāṃ, tārām iva gurukalatropaśobhitāṃ, śatakoṭimūrtim iva muṣṭigrāhyamadhyāṃ, priyaṅguśyāmāsakhīm iva priyadarśanāṃ, brahmadattamahiṣīm iva somaprabhāṃ, diggajakareṇukām ivānupamāṃ, velām iva tamālapatrasādhitāṃ, aśvatarakanyām iva madālasāṃ Vāsavadattāṃ dadarśa |
children.translated_text: 'You are running — when the liquid torrent is released, is this restless one acting capriciously? This flower-cluster has fallen from your ear! <s>Surekhe</s> (O beautifully-lined one), you are adorned with the beauty befitting one worthy of being implored by the gods (<s>sura</s>) for wine (<s>surā</s>)! Intoxicated in the quarrel, with the tinkling of your golden girdle-chains, you seem to challenge <s>Smara</s> (the Love-god)! <s>Malaye</s> (O sandalwood one), with your gaze alone you have obtained what is desired on Mount <s>Malaya</s>! <s>Kalike</s> (O bud-like one), release this clamorous girdle — listen to the soft melody of the <s>vallakī</s> (lute)! My girdle is not treacherous (<s>khalā</s>) — it is you alone who are noisy! <s>Utkālike</s> (O wave-like one), your longing (<s>utkalikā</s>) is a great wave! What comparison can reach the drinking-beauty of the eyes in your face — even the moon falls short! In your heart, O faithful one, someone seems to dwell! <s>Kerali</s> (O Kerala maiden), this mass of braided hair, bearing heavy garlands of blooming jasmine, rivals a terrible monsoon cloud-fragment! <s>Kuntalike</s> (O curly-locked one), singing voices are heard near the city gate-towers — why do you delay a moment from glancing? And you playfully trouble the flirtatious company of friends! <s>Murale</s> (O flute-like one), the happiness gained in the striking of breasts, the joy that removes Love's fever — she, now separated from him, why do you grieve? Your departed lover remembers the skill of <s>Rati</s> (love's pleasure). The nail-wound on a night born of Love causes her no pain! Why are the eyes not drinking in the moment that delights all people? Dear friend <s>Madanamālini</s> (O garland-of-Love), cease from the longing for the union of ruby lips! <s>Kuraṅgike</s> (O fawn-like one), prepare sprouts of grass for the fawn-children! <s>Kiśorike</s> (O young-colt one), arrange the watching of the young colts! <s>Taralike</s> (O tremulous one), fan out the dense, heavy incense-clouds! <s>Karpūrike</s> (O camphor one), whiten the burden of your breasts with camphor dust! <s>Mātaṅgike</s> (O elephant-maiden), honor the request of the baby elephant! <s>Śaśilekhe</s> (O moon-lined one), draw a crescent moon on your forehead! <s>Ketakike</s> (O screwpine one), prepare the <s>ketakī</s>-bower for the longing! <s>Śakunike</s> (O bird-maiden), give food to the pet birds! <s>Madanamañjari</s> (O Love's-blossom), adorn the plantain-chamber of the assembly hall with flower-sprays! <s>Śṛṅgāramañjari</s> (O beauty-blossom), plan the decoration of love! <s>Sañjīvanike</s> (O life-giving one), offer pepper-leaves to the <s>jīvajīvaka</s> bird-pair! <s>Pallavike</s> (O shoot-like one), fashion an artificial <s>ketakī</s>-grove with camphor dust! <s>Sahakāramañjari</s> (O mango-blossom), infuse the mango fragrance into the fan-breezes! <s>Madanalekhe</s> (O Love-letter), write a love-letter to the mountain breeze! <s>Makarike</s> (O crocodile-maiden), give lotus-stalk sprouts to the royal goslings! <s>Vilāsavati</s> (O graceful one), make the young peacock dance! <s>Tamālike</s> (O <s>tamāla</s>-tree one), perfume the courtyard with sandalwood paste! <s>Kāñcanike</s> (O golden one), sprinkle musk-liquid in the golden pavilion! <s>Pravālike</s> (O coral one), water the young coral-grove with saffron-juice!' — Hearing such conversations of the maidens, tender with mutual affection, <s>Kandarpaketu</s> together with <s>Makaranda</s> marveled in his mind: 'Oh, the surpassing beauty of these palaces! Oh, the skill in the art of love's adornment!' And thinking thus — 'There is that pavilion built of ivory, lovely as the <s>Mālavī</s> teeth gently bitten in play at that moment; and that pet parrot confined in a cage made of camphor-sticks' — and entering, he beheld <s>Vāsavadattā</s>, who was resplendent with a pair of legs [beautiful] like grammar with its reddened feet (also: passionate <s>pādas</s>), like the <s>Bhārata</s> [epic] with its excellent <s>parvans</s> (joints/chapters), like the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s> with its beautiful <s>Sundarakāṇḍa</s> (chapter/thigh); slim-waisted like the study of meters (<s>chandoviciti</s>); whose hands and ears deserved enumeration like the science of stars (<s>nakṣatravidyā</s>); whose nature illuminated like the system of logic (<s>Nyāya</s>) with its <s>Udyotakara</s>; adorned with ornaments like a Buddhist council (<s>saṅgīti</s>); illuminating a blissful self like an <s>Upaniṣad</s>; of beautiful feet like the tradition of the twice-born (<s>dvija</s>); of beautiful hips like the beauty of the <s>Vindhya</s> mountain; adorned by a great spouse like <s>Tārā</s> (the star/Bṛhaspati's wife); of waist graspable in a fist like a figure of a hundred <s>koṭis</s>; lovely to behold like a friend dark as <s>priyangu</s> (millet); radiant with moonlight like <s>Brahmadatta's</s> queen <s>Somaprabhā</s>; incomparable like the she-elephant of the world-elephant; prepared with <s>tamāla</s>-leaf decoration like the seashore (<s>velā</s>); languid with passion like a daughter of the <s>Aśvatara</s> [serpent-race] — he beheld <s>Vāsavadattā</s>.

children.text: atha prītivisphāritena cakṣuṣā pibataḥ Kandarpaketor jahāra cetanāṃ mūrcchāvegaḥ | tam api paśyantī Vāsavadattā mumūrccha | atha Makarandasakhījanaprayatnalabdhasaṃjñau tau ekāsanam alaṃcakratuḥ | tato Vāsavadattāyāḥ prāṇebhyo 'pi garīyasī sarvavisrambhapātraṃ Kalāvatī nāma Kandarpaketum uvāca | "āryaputra nāyaṃ visrambhakathānām avasaraḥ | ato laghutaram evābhidhīyate | tvatkṛte yānayā vedanānubhūtā sā yadi nabhaḥ patrāyate sāgaro lolāyate brahmā lipikarāyate bhujagapatir vākkathakaḥ tadā kim api katham apy ekaikair yugasahasrair abhilikhyate kathyate vā | tvayā ca rājyam ujjhitam | kiṃ bahunātmā saṅkaṭe samāropitaḥ | eṣāsmatsvāmiduhitā prabhātāyāṃ rajanyāṃ pitrā yauvanātikramadoṣaśaṅkinā bhayena vidyādharacakravartino Vijayaketoḥ putrāya Puṣpaketave pāṇigrahaṇāya dātavyā | anayāpy ālocitam adya yadi taṃ janam ādāya nāgacchati Tamālikā, tadāvaśyam eva mayā hutavahe śayitavyam" iti | tad asyāḥ sukṛtavaśena mahābhāgaḥ imāṃ bhūmim anuprāptaḥ | atha Kandarpaketur bhītabhītaḥ sapraṇayam ānandāmṛtasāgaroddāmataraṅgalaharībhir āpluta iva Vāsavadattāyā sahāmantrya Makarandaṃ vārtānveṣaṇāya tatraiva nagare niyujya, bhujageneva sadāgatyabhimukhena Manojavanāmnā turagena tayā saha nagarān niragāt |
children.translated_text: Then, as <s>Kandarpaketu</s> was drinking [the sight of her] with eyes wide open in delight, a rush of fainting seized his consciousness. <s>Vāsavadattā</s> too, beholding him, fainted. Then, having been revived through the efforts of <s>Makaranda</s> and the company of friends, the two adorned a single seat. Then the one named <s>Kalāvatī</s>, dearer to <s>Vāsavadattā</s> than her own life and the vessel of all her confidence, spoke to <s>Kandarpaketu</s>: 'Noble sir, this is not the occasion for intimate conversation. Therefore let it be said most briefly. The suffering she has endured on your account — if the sky were to become a page, the ocean a pen, <s>Brahmā</s> the scribe, and the lord of serpents the narrator, then perhaps somehow, over thousands of ages one by one, it might be written or told. And you have abandoned your kingdom. In short, the self has been placed in peril. This daughter of our lord is to be given at dawn by her father — who fears the fault of her youth passing by — in marriage to <s>Puṣpaketu</s>, the son of <s>Vijayaketu</s>, the <s>Vidyādhara</s> emperor. She too has resolved: if <s>Tamālikā</s> does not bring that person today, then I must surely lay myself upon the fire.' Therefore, by the power of her merit, the most fortunate one has arrived at this place.' Then <s>Kandarpaketu</s>, trembling with excitement, as if inundated by the surging waves of the ocean of the nectar of bliss, having lovingly taken leave of <s>Vāsavadattā</s> and having assigned <s>Makaranda</s> to gathering news right there in the city, departed from the city with her upon a horse named <s>Manojavana</s> (swift-as-thought), [a steed swift as] a serpent always facing the direction of the wind.

children.translated_text: And gradually, having passed through a cremation ground — crowded with fearless flocks of birds gathering to seize morsels of flesh from corpses; terrifying with hideous <s>Kaṭapūtanā</s>, <s>Uttāla</s>, <s>Vetāla</s>, and other spectral beings, hissing amidst the half-burnt funeral pyre circles of dreadful thirst-driven ghouls; repulsive with the earth filled with heaps of buzzing carrion-flies fallen upon the sheets of blood from the severed noses, ears, and limbs of doubtful merit impaled on stake-tips; fearsome with the terrifying cracking sounds of skulls being split by the fierce fire of the pyre; like [a realm of] <s>Śūlapāṇi</s> (<s>Śiva</s>), with a body surrounded by skull-offerings, ashes, <s>Śiva</s>-fire, sacred ash, and serpents; like a superhuman being, served by many circles — having traveled what seemed like hundreds of leagues in the blink of an eye, [they] entered the <s>Vindhya</s> forest — like the shore at the time of cosmic dissolution, with hosts of gathered suns; like the state of a <s>Nāga</s>-kingdom, of infinite roots; like <s>Sudharmā</s> (Indra's assembly hall), with <s>Kauśika</s> (Indra/owls) freely stationed; like the service of the virtuous, rich in <s>śrīphala</s> (bilva fruit, also: the fruit of prosperity); like the battlefield of the <s>Bhārata</s> war, with distant-sprouting <s>arjuna</s> trees (also: the hero <s>Arjuna</s>); like the state of <s>Puloman</s>'s family, with <s>Indrāṇikā</s> suitable for the thousand-eyed one; like the mental disposition of <s>Śūrapāla</s>, adorned with <s>gaṇikārikā</s> (courtesans/a type of plant); like the prosperity of the good, with <s>aśoka</s>, <s>sarala</s> (pine), and <s>punnāga</s> (mast-wood) trees in bloom; like the play of children, supported by a nurse (<s>dhātrī</s>/myrobalan tree); somewhere like the disposition of <s>Rāghava</s> (<s>Rāma</s>), pervaded by <s>Vaidehī</s> (<s>Sītā</s>/a type of earth); somewhere like the churning of the milk-ocean, with <s>amṛta</s> (nectar/a plant) bursting forth; somewhere like the power of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, freely invincible (<s>aparājitā</s>, also: a creeper); somewhere like the poetry of <s>Vālmīki</s>, showing the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> dynasty (also: sugarcane groves); like <s>Laṅkā</s>, adorned with abundant <s>palāśa</s> (flame-of-the-forest) trees; like the <s>Dhārtarāṣṭra</s> army, surrounded by showers of <s>Arjuna</s>'s arrows (also: <s>arjuna</s> trees); like the form of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, of many forms; like <s>Sugrīva</s>'s army, attended by <s>panasa</s> (jackfruit), <s>candana</s> (sandalwood), <s>nala</s> (reed), and <s>kumuda</s> (water-lily) trees; somewhere like a widow, adorned with vermilion marks and coral ornaments; somewhere like the <s>Kuru</s> army, accompanied by <s>Ulūka</s>, <s>Droṇa</s>, and <s>Śakuni</s> (also: owls, hawks, and birds) together with the sons of <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> (also: <s>dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> geese); though adorned with unfading <s>jāti</s> (jasmine/caste), of hostile lineage (bamboo); though offering fearlessness, terrifying; though always wholesome and beneficial, with overgrown <s>gulma</s> (shrubs/tumors); though pervaded by <s>ṣaṭpada</s> (six-footed bees), disturbed by <s>dvipada</s> (bipeds/humans); though adorned by twice-born (<s>dvija</s>, birds/Brahmins), of ignoble lineage (bamboo/clan).

dhvajapaṭapallaveṣu, phalapāka iva karkandhuṣu, kuṅkumacchaṭārasa iva vyomasaudhāṅgaṇasya, sañcaradaruṇayavanikāpaṭa iva kālasya, bālapravālabhaṅgāruṇe prasaraty ātape, kṣaṇena ca cakravākacakravālahṛdayaśokasantāpaharaṇād iva, dahanasamanupraveśād iva, dinanāthakāntopalasaṅgamād iva, uttiṣṭhamānam uṣnam uṣṇaraśmer āśrayati raśmisañcaye Kandarpaketuḥ sarvarātrajāgaraparavaśa āhāraśūnyaśarīratayā niścetanaḥ, anekayojanaśatabhramaṇakhinnaḥ, Vāsavadattayāpy evaṃvidhayā saha latāgṛhe mandamārutāndolitakusumaparimalalubdhamukharaparibhramadbhramarajhaṅkāramanohare tatkālasulabhayā nidrayā gṛhīto niṣpandakaraṇagrāmaḥ suṣvāpa |
children.translated_text: Gradually, as the host of stars was being carried off, like a school of living fish being dragged in a net cast by the fisherman of Time into the great lake of the sky using the dark [net]; as the lotus-pool, opening with its red garments (petals), seemed to recite properly-metered verses with the deep buzzing of bees drunk from sipping clusters of honey-drops, the opened lotus-blossoms attended by hundred-petaled manuscripts of leaf and stem guided by the arrow-device of irregularly grown fiber-creepers; as the lotus-bed, like a beggar-farmer of Time, seemed to offer incense to the blessed garland-of-rays (<s>Sūrya</s>) under the pretext of erect lotuses followed by a mass of bee-swarms accompanied by the murmur of pollen-dust, while dense petal-vessels closed around the bees in the thick honeyed mire of fragrant filaments like [planting] seeds of darkness; as the moon [looked] like a mortar whose interior was cracked and dented by the blows of falling pestles dislodged from the pair of hands of the bride of Night; as the star-clusters twinkled like grains of rice scattered from pounding; as the day-monkey, with a dawn-reddened face, ascended the tree of the sky, and as the constellations fell from the shaking branches like the directions, and the star-clusters like scattered blossoms and the moon-disc like a fruit [falling]; as the ground of the sky, speckled with star-grains, [waited] for the day-rooster with its beautiful face crested with youthful reddish hues to descend and strut upon it; as the eastern quarter seemed to laugh, [saying] 'This twice-born lord (<s>dvijapatī</s> — the moon, also: the lord of Brahmins), well-known for his association with me, will fall from his contact with <s>Vāruṇī</s> (liquor/the western quarter)'; with streams of blood from the elephant of darkness slain by the blow of his hand (rays), or as if washed by mineral-pigment streams from the waterfalls of the eastern mountain's peak, or like the sheen of rubies split by the prancing sharp hooves of the galloping horse, or like the streams of blood flowing from the head of a maddened elephant struck by the lion's paw, or as if with the juice of passion-redness from the power to accomplish the affairs of the three worlds — the blessed <s>Bhāskara</s> (Sun), his disc red, with hands stretched out as if to seize the garden of star-lilies, saffron-dye-red, appearing on the hood-jewel of the great serpent of the Eastern Mountain, offered to the voluptuous lady of the East, like a golden bud on the sapphire sky, like a golden pinnacle-pot of the city-wall of the sky-city, like a moist saffron-drop on the forehead of the East, like a single flower on the young creeper of the dawn, like a string of madder-red thread, like a dawn-red garland strung, like a golden wonder-pill of the day-<s>vidyādhara</s>, like the sole of the foot of the directional elephant reddened with mineral pigment — the blessed Sun ascended into view, the thief of the darkness of night; spreading redness like a madder-red yak-tail fan over the directional elephants; like an outpouring of blood from the battle of the <s>Mahābhārata</s> over <s>Kurukṣetra</s>; like a coating of rainbow-luster over the gaps in the clouds; like a saffron robe in the monasteries of the <s>Śākya</s> (Buddhist) order; like a <s>kusumbha</s> (safflower) dye on flag-cloth banners; like the ripeness of fruit upon <s>karkandhū</s> (jujube) trees; like a stream of saffron-paste upon the courtyard of the sky-mansion; like a moving reddish curtain-cloth of Time — as the sunshine spread, ruddy as the breaking of young coral. And in an instant, <s>Kandarpaketu</s>, as if overwhelmed by the removal of the heart-grief of the circle of <s>cakravāka</s> (ruddy geese); as if by the mutual entry of fire (<s>sahagamana</s>); as if from the contact of the beloved sun-gem — feeling the rising heat from the gathering of the sun's rays, overcome by wakefulness throughout the entire night, his body emptied of food, senseless, exhausted from wandering hundreds of leagues, together with <s>Vāsavadattā</s> who was in a similar state, in a bower of creepers charming with the buzzing of bees circling about, lured by the fragrance of flowers swayed by the gentle breeze — seized by sleep that was easy to come by at that hour, with his entire faculty of senses stilled, he fell fast asleep.

children.translated_text: Then, when the sun's disc had risen to the zenith — like a merchant who had spread out his wares, like a great forest-fire illuminating all wooden things — <s>Kandarpaketu</s>, finding the bower empty without his beloved, rose up, and casting his gaze about — now at the tree-trunks, now at the treetops, now in the blind wells, now in the heaps of dry leaves, now at the sky, now in the directions, now in the intermediate directions — wandering about with his heart burning unceasingly, he lamented.

sāpasāram iva phenaiḥ, sasurāmodam iva velābakulagandhaiḥ, saroṣam iva garjitaiḥ, sakhedam iva niḥśvasitaiḥ, sabhrūkuṭībandham iva taraṅgaiḥ, ālānastambham iva rāmasetunā, kumbhīnasīkukṣim iva lavaṇotpattisthānaṃ, vyākaraṇam iva vitatastrīnadīkṛtyabahulaṃ, rājakulam iva dṛśyamānamahāpātraṃ, hastibandham iva vārigatānekanāgamucyamānaśūtkāraṃ, viśvāmitraputravargam ivāmbhojacārumatsyopaśobhitaṃ, satpuruṣam iva gotrāśrayaṃ sādhum ivācyutasthitiramaṇīyaṃ, sanṛpam iva sajjanakramakaraṃ, kṛtamanyum iva karatoyāplutamukhaṃ, virahiṇam iva candanodakasiktaṃ, vilāsinam iva narmadāvagataṃ, uddhṛtakālakūṭam api prakaṭitaviśarāśiṃ, ativṛddham api sundarīparigatakaṇṭhaṃ, surotpattisthānam apy asurādhiṣṭhānaṃ jalanidhim apaśyat |
children.translated_text: 'Alas, beloved <s>Vāsavadattā</s>, grant me your sight! Why have you disappeared as a jest? The sufferings I have endured for your sake — you yourself are the witness. Dear friend <s>Makaranda</s>, behold the cruel sport of fate upon me! Have I not performed meritorious deeds? Cruel is the ripening of destiny! Insurmountable is the course of ill fortune! Ah, how exceedingly bitter is the sidelong glance of the planets! Ah, the blessings of elders bear fruit unlike [what was expected]! Ah, the evil dreams and ill omens have borne fruit! In every way, nothing is beyond the reach of what must be. Were not the sciences properly studied? Were not the teachers duly worshipped? Were not the sacred fires duly attended? Were not the deities duly honored? Were the earth-deities slighted? Were the cows not circumambulated? Was no refuge given to one seeking shelter?' — lamenting thus in many ways, he emerged to the south through a forest — dense with fresh <s>nala</s> (reeds), <s>nalada</s> (spikenard), lotuses, <s>nīcula</s> (barringtonia), <s>picula</s>, and <s>viḍūḍa</s> trees; its outskirts blocked by abundant <s>ciribilva</s>, <s>bilva</s> (wood-apple), <s>uṭaja</s> (hermitages), and <s>kuṭaja</s> (indrajava) trees; with lovely <s>sundarī</s> groves resounding with the eager cries of <s>bhṛṅgarāja</s> (paradise flycatcher) birds; with swarms of bees clustering upon the trunks of young <s>varuṇa</s> trees shielded by extensive spreads of <s>vetasa</s> (cane) groves; its tree-grounds moistened by the dripping honey-masses broken by long-tailed <s>golāṅgūla</s> (langur) monkeys; dense with <s>tāla</s> (palm), <s>hintāla</s> (date palm), <s>pūga</s> (areca), <s>punnāga</s>, and <s>nāgakesara</s> (ironwood) trees; thick with groves of camphor, jasmine, <s>ketaka</s> (screwpine), <s>kovidāra</s> (orchid tree), <s>mandāra</s>, <s>bījapūraka</s> (citron), <s>jambīra</s> (lemon), and <s>jambū</s> (rose-apple) bushes; whose <s>nandīnala</s> reed bowers were filled with the cooing calls of <s>pratyūha</s> and <s>dātyūha</s> (gallinule) flocks; whose luxuriant mango branches were perched upon by heaps of bold, melodious-throated peacocks; bustling with families of restless chickens from households of nests; whose <s>kurabaka</s> (red amaranth) rows bristled with horripilation from clusters of buds; its ten directions stained with the beauty of red <s>aśoka</s> blossoms; with the increasing dusty haze of the day from the scattering of pollen from fully opened <s>kesara</s> (stamens); where people's delight was produced by the sweet jingling of bees joining the saffron-yellow flower-clusters; where fearless elephants scratched their itching flanks against the trunks of <s>mucukunda</s> trees darkened by their rut-fluid; whose <s>kuṭaja</s> tree-hollows were made nesting-places by hens that had hatched a few days before; where no flattery was performed by the chattering sparrows carrying clever vocal mimics; with the pecking beaks of sharp <s>cakora</s> (partridge) birds walking alongside companion-birds; with hare-kittens sleeping comfortably on the delicate stone-surfaces of <s>śaileya</s> (mountain-moss) rocks; with heaps of <s>gaudhera</s> (civet) animals dwelling confidently in the root-crevices of <s>śephālikā</s> (night-jasmine) plants; with undisturbed <s>raṅku</s> (antelope); with undisturbed mongooses at play; with the sprouting of mango buds swallowed by melodious cuckoo-flocks; with <s>camara</s> (yak) herds ruminating in the mango groves; resounding with a noise like drums from the ear-flapping of herds of elephants lulled to drowsiness by the cascading-waterfall sounds of mountain-streams near <s>nīḍa</s> (nest) hills pleasing to the ear; with herds of <s>ruru</s> (a kind of deer) delighting in the song of nearby <s>kinnarī</s> (celestial) women; with rows of young boar-piglets whose scratchings were dyed by the flow of turmeric juice from crushed green [turmeric]; born with flocks of buzzing <s>jāhaka</s> birds among heaps of <s>guñjā</s> (rosary peas); crowded with the husks of <s>pāṭala</s> (trumpet-flower) beetle-cases split open by the cheek-pouches of baby monkeys angered by their teeth [teething]; with a splendid group of resplendent-maned lions whose beautiful manes were spattered with streams of blood from maddened elephants slashed by the brutal slaps of their exceedingly sharp nail-tips like the edges of thunderbolts — having traveled some distance near the shore of the great ocean, he beheld the ocean — which, through its excessively restless waves surging in heaps, seemed unskilled in imitating the furious dance of destruction with arms wielding axes; delightful at its borders with lines of foam like victory-banners of <s>Vāruṇī</s> (the goddess of wine), or like garlands of shed serpent-skins of <s>Śeṣa's</s> clan, or like continuous streams of the residual atoms of the moon; as if another sky descending upon the earth's surface, enticing the sky-dwellers with pearls (resembling pearl-drops) from the shower of spray-drops leaping up from the gleaming ocean; whose belly-region was filled with many winged mountains that had come seeking refuge; dug out by the sons of <s>Sagara</s>; from which the <s>Pārijāta</s> tree had been extracted; the birthplace of jewel-gems; teeming with herds of elephantine sea-creatures (<s>makara</s>); eager for the fish-morsels as prey; with circling crocodile-wheels moving about; whose groves of <s>kandalī</s>, <s>lavaṅga</s> (cloves), <s>mātuluṅga</s> (citron), and bushes were stirred by the undulations of rings of submerged <s>timiṅgila</s> (whale) herds; whose shore-sandbanks of young water-moss were trampled by pairs of water-men (<s>jalamānuṣa</s>) tossed about by the restless waters agitated by the wind of waves; whose bank-ledges were etched by the sharp nails of conch-shells whose mouths were scratched on the hard rocks of coral-tip-split [formations]; whose waters were crowded with the fleet of leaf-boats of <s>Khageśvara</s> (<s>Garuḍa's</s>) lineage; as if still bearing the effects of the churning of <s>Mandara</s> in its whirlpool-rotations; as if bearing remorse in its foam; as if bearing the fragrance of liquor in the scents of the <s>bakula</s> groves along its shores; as if roaring with anger; as if sighing with sorrow; as if having knitted brows in its waves; as if having a hitching-post in <s>Rāma's</s> bridge; whose salt-production site was like the belly of a <s>kumbhīnasī</s> (alligator-snout); like grammar, extensive with feminine, river, and verbal forms; like a royal court, with its great vessels (<s>mahāpātra</s>) on display; like an elephant-stable, whose trumpeting arose from many water-serpents being released; like the progeny of <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, beautified by lotus-lovely fish; like a virtuous person, taking refuge in lineage; like a saint, beautified by the steady abiding of <s>Acyuta</s> (<s>Viṣṇu</s>); like a king, with the succession of good people as crocodiles; like one angry, with its face bathed by the waters of <s>Karatoyā</s> (a river); like one in separation, sprinkled with sandalwood water; like a gallant, visited by the <s>Narmadā</s>; though having extracted the <s>Kālakūṭa</s> poison, displaying heaps of venom; though exceedingly aged, with beautiful women clasping its neck; though the birthplace of liquor (<s>surā</s>), also the abode of demons (<s>asura</s>) — he beheld this ocean.

children.text: acintayac ca "aho me kṛtāpakāreṇāpi vidhinopakṛtir eva kṛtā yad ayaṃ locanagocaratāṃ nītaḥ samudraḥ | tad atra deham utsṛjya priyāvirahāgniṃ nirvāpayāmi | yady apy anāturasyātmatyāgo na vihitas tathāpi kāryaḥ | na khalu sarvaḥ sarvaṃ kāryam akāryaṃ vā karoti | asāre saṃsāre kena kiṃ nāma na kṛtam | tathā hi | gurudāraharaṇaṃ dvijarājo 'karot | purūravā brāhmaṇadhanatṛṣṇayā vinanāśa | nahuṣaḥ parakalatradohadī mahābhujaga āsīt | yayātir āhitapāṇigrahaṇaḥ papāta | sudyumnaḥ strīmaya ivābhavat | somasya prakhyātā jantuvadhanirghṛṇatā | purukutsaḥ kutsita ivāsīt | kuvalayāśvo nāśvatarakanyām api parijahāra | nṛgaḥ kṛkalāsatām agamat | nalaṃ kalir abhibhūtavān | saṃvaraṇo mitraduhitari viklavatām agāt | daśaratha iṣṭarāmonmādena mṛtyum avāpa | kārtavīryo gobrāhmaṇapīḍayā pañcatvam ayāsīt | manuḥ suvarṇavyasanī nanāśa | śantanur ativyasanād vipine vilalāpa | yudhiṣṭhiraḥ samaraśirasi satyam utsasarja | nāsty akalaṅkaḥ ko 'pi prāyaḥ | dehatyāge na kalaṅkī bhavāmīti" vicintya kurarakharanakharaśikharakhaṇḍitapṛthulapṛthuromāvilam, aviralaśakulaśalkasaṅkulajalanakulakuloccāraṃ, kroṣṭukulocchiṣṭhavikaṭakarkaṭakarparaparamparāparigataprāntam, atitaralatarajalarayalulitacaṭulaśapharakulakavalanakṛtam, atinibhṛtabakaśakuninivahadhavalitaparisaram, aticapalajalakapikulaviharaṇalulitasalilakaṇanikarajaḍitaparimalitaśiśiritam, anudivasanipatadatitaruṇavanamahiṣaśṛṅgaśikharalikhitaviṣamataṭam, anavaratacaradasitamukhacaraṇavihaganivahamadhuraninadamukharitam, ahimakarakiraṇarucijalamanujaśayanamṛditajaladharaṇītalam, atibahalamadajalaśabalakaraṭataṭakarivaraśatanipatitamadhukaranikaramadhuravirutaratakaram, atijavanapavanavidhutajalavinaṭananipatitamaṇigaṇaparigataparisaraṃ, jalanidhibhujaganirmuktanirmokapaṭṭam iva, darpaṇam iva vasundharāyāḥ, sphaṭikakuṭṭimam iva varuṇasya pulinatalam āsasāda |
children.translated_text: And he reflected: 'Ah, even fate, though having wronged me, has actually done me a favor by bringing this ocean within the range of my eyes. Here I shall abandon my body and extinguish the fire of separation from my beloved. Even though self-destruction is not prescribed for one who is not mortally ill, it must be done nonetheless. Not everyone does everything proper or improper. In this essenceless worldly existence, what has not been done by whom? For: the king of the twice-born [the moon, or <s>Bṛhaspati</s>] committed the abduction of his teacher's wife. <s>Purūravas</s> perished through greed for a <s>brāhmaṇa's</s> wealth. <s>Nahuṣa</s>, desirous of another's wife, became a great serpent. <s>Yayāti</s>, though his marriage-vow had been taken, fell. <s>Sudyumna</s> became as if made into a woman. <s>Soma's</s> cruelty in slaying his offspring is well known. <s>Purukutsa</s> was despicable. <s>Kuvalayāśva</s> did not even spare a donkey-maiden. <s>Nṛga</s> became a chameleon. <s>Kali</s> overpowered <s>Nala</s>. <s>Saṃvaraṇa</s> became distraught over the daughter of his friend [the Sun]. <s>Daśaratha</s> died of the madness of longing for his beloved <s>Rāma</s>. <s>Kārtavīrya</s> met his end through oppressing cows and <s>brāhmaṇas</s>. <s>Manu</s> perished through addiction to gold. <s>Śantanu</s>, through excessive addiction, lamented in the forest. <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> abandoned truth on the battlefield. There is hardly anyone without blemish. By abandoning my body, I shall not become stained' — having thus resolved, he reached the sandy shore — which was [adorned] by the fish-scales of dense <s>śakula</s> (fish) stirred by the sharp nail-tips of <s>kurara</s> (osprey) birds whose broad feathers were disheveled; with the droppings of mongoose families amid the fish-filled waters; its edges strewn with rows of hideous crab-shells, leftovers of jackals; made by the swallowing of darting schools of restless fish tossed by the excessively turbulent water-currents; its surroundings whitened by flocks of exceedingly still herons; cooled and stiffened by showers of water-drops scattered by the play of excessively restless water-monkey troops; its uneven banks scratched by the horn-tips of young wild buffaloes descending daily; resounding with the sweet calls of flocks of birds whose beaks and feet were revealed as they fed constantly; its ground-surface trodden by the sleeping forms of water-men on beds of water glittering with the rays of the unclouded sun; delightful with the sweet cries of hundreds of fine elephants whose temples were mottled with excessively copious rut-fluid, upon whom swarms of bees had descended; its surroundings bordered by heaps of fallen gems from the water stirred by the exceedingly swift wind — [a shore] like a shed serpent-skin of the ocean-serpent; like a mirror of the earth; like a crystal pavement of <s>Varuṇa</s> — he reached that sandy shore.

children.text: tataḥ kṛtasnānādir jalam avataritum ārebhe śarīratyāgāya |
children.translated_text: Then, having completed his ablutions and other [rites], he began to enter the water for the purpose of abandoning his body.

children.text: atha sānugraheṣu grāheṣu, nirmatsareṣumatsyeṣu, akṣudreṣu kṣudreṣu, vatsaleṣu kacchapeṣu, akrūreṣu nakreṣu, abhayaṅkareṣu makareṣu, amāreṣu śiśumāreṣu, ākāśāt Sarasvatī samudacarat | "ārya Kandarpaketo punar api tava priyayā saṃgamo bhaviṣyatīty acireṇa | tad virama maraṇavyavasāyād" iti | tad upaśrutya maraṇārambhād virarāma | punaḥ priyayā samāgamāśayā saṃsthitihetubhūtam aśanaṃ cikīrṣuḥ kacchopāntabhuvaṃ jagāma | tatra tata itaḥ paribhraman phalamūlādinā vane vartayan kālaṃ nināya |
children.translated_text: Then, amidst crocodiles that were gracious (<s>sānugraha</s>, pun: grāha = crocodile), fish that were free of envy (<s>nirmatsara</s>, pun: matsya = fish), small creatures that were not petty (<s>akṣudra</s>, pun: kṣudra = small fish), turtles that were affectionate (<s>vatsala</s>, pun: kacchapa = turtle), crocodiles that were not cruel (<s>akrūra</s>, pun: nakra = crocodile), sea-monsters that were fearless (<s>abhayaṅkara</s>, pun: makara = sea-monster), and porpoises that were not deadly (<s>amāra</s>, pun: śiśumāra = porpoise) — <s>Sarasvatī</s> (the goddess of speech) arose from the sky: 'Noble <s>Kandarpaketu</s>, you shall soon be reunited with your beloved! Therefore cease from your resolve to die.' Hearing this, he desisted from his attempt at death. With the hope of reunion with his beloved, desiring to eat food that would sustain his life, he went to the riverbank. There, wandering here and there, subsisting on fruits and roots in the forest, he passed the time.

children.text: ekadā tu katipayamāsāpagame kākalīgāyana iva samṛddhanimnagānadaḥ, sandhyāsamaya iva nartitanīlakaṇṭhaḥ, kumāramayūra iva samūḍhaśarajanmā, mahātapasvīva praśamitarajaḥprasaraḥ, tāpasa iva dhṛtajaladakarakaḥ, pralayakāla iva darśitānekataraṇivibhramaḥ, nirupadravakānanoddeśa iva ghanotsukitasāraṅgaḥ, revatīkarapallava iva halidhṛtakaraḥ ājagāma varṣāsamayaḥ |
children.translated_text: Then one day, after the passage of several months, the rainy season arrived — like a singer of <s>kākalī</s> (soft melodies) with its abundant river-songs; like the twilight hour, making the peacocks (<s>nīlakaṇṭha</s>) dance; like a young peacock, whose birth from the arrow (<s>śara</s>) is well-known; like a great ascetic, having calmed the spread of dust (<s>rajas</s>, also: passion); like a hermit, holding a water-pot (<s>karakā</s>) of clouds; like the time of cosmic dissolution (<s>pralaya</s>), displaying the confusion of many boats; like a peaceful forest region, where the <s>sāraṅga</s> (cuckoo) is excited by the clouds; like the shoot-hands of <s>Revatī</s>, held by the ploughman (<s>Balarāma</s>).

children.text: nirbhinnameghanīlotpalakānane krīḍāsarasīva nabhasi smarasya ratnanaukeva, kulaṭalakṣmīmātaṅgakanyānartanacalarajjur iva, nabhaḥsaudhatoraṇamālikeva, pravasatānidāghena divaḥpayodhare smaraṇāya kṣatā nakhapadāvalir iva, gaganalakṣmīratnaraśanāmāleva, nabhomandārakusumamañjarīva, ratinakhamārjanaratnaśalākeva, ratnaśuktir iva kusumaketor indradhanurlatā rarāja |
children.translated_text: In the sky, like a pleasure-lake in a grove of cloud-dark blue lotuses (<s>nīlotpala</s>), like a jeweled boat of <s>Smara</s> (the Love-god), like a rope for the dancing of the wanton <s>Lakṣmī</s>'s elephant-daughter, like a garland of arches of the sky-palace, like a row of nail-marks scratched in remembrance on the breast of heaven by the departing summer, like a jeweled girdle-chain of the beauty of the sky, like a cluster of celestial <s>mandāra</s> flowers, like a jeweled stick for polishing <s>Rati's</s> nails, like a pearl-shell — the rainbow-creeper of <s>Kusumaketu</s> (the Flower-bannered Love-god) shone brilliantly.

children.text: ativeganipītajaladhiśaṅkhamālām iva balākācchalād udvamann ivādṛśyata jaladharanikaraḥ | āpītaharitaiḥ kṛṣṇāsu kedārikākoṣṭhikāsu samutphaladbhir jātuśabalair iva dardurair vidyutā samaṃ cikrīḍa varṣākālaḥ | ravidīpakajjalanicayanikaṣopala iva meghe samayasuvarṇakāranikaṣitasuvarṇalekheva taḍid aśobhata | virahiṇāṃ hṛdayaṃ vidārayituṃ karapatram iva kusumāyudhasya krakacacchadam aśobhata | jaladadāruṇi lolataḍillatāpatranipātavidārite vegadhūtāś cūrṇacayā iva jalareṇavo babhuḥ | vicchinnadigvadhūhāramukta iva kharapavanavegabhramitaghanagharaghaṭṭanasañcūrṇitās tārānikarā iva bhuvanavijigīṣor makaradhvajasya prasthānalājāñjalaya iva karakā vyarājanta |
children.translated_text: The mass of clouds appeared to vomit, under the pretext of white cranes (<s>balākā</s>), what seemed like garlands of conch-shells swallowed from the ocean at great speed. The rainy season sported with lightning together with frogs — speckled like lac-insects, leaping up in the black compartments of paddy fields, yellow-green in hue. Lightning gleamed on the cloud like a streak of gold tested on the touchstone of a seasonal goldsmith, upon the touchstone-mass of soot from the sun's lamp. Like a saw-blade, the leaf-weapon of <s>Kusumāyudha</s> (the Flower-weaponed Love-god) gleamed to rend the hearts of those separated [from their beloveds]. In the cloud-wood, split by the falling of the flickering lightning-creeper blade, water-sprays flew about like sawdust shaken by force. Hailstones (<s>karakā</s>) shone magnificently — like scattered pearls from the broken necklace of the Directions-bride, like crushed star-clusters ground by the clash of violently wind-whirled dense clouds, like handfuls of parched rice offered at the departure-ceremony of <s>Makaradhvaja</s> (the Love-god) on his world-conquering campaign.

children.text: anantaram akhañjakhañjarīṭe 'kuñcitakrauñcasañcāre, nirbharabharadvājadvijavācāṭaviṭape, pātrabhrāntaśukakalamakedāre, praveśitāveśikarājahaṃse, kaṃsāridehadyutidyutale, haṃsatūlatulitarājajjalamuci, sāndrīkṛtendumahākāmukamudi, madhuramadhutṛṇavīrudhi, sarasasārasarasitasārakāsāre, kaśerukandalubdhapotripotapautrotkhātataṭataḍāgasañcaranmāṣaputrikāpatrīpaṭalamadhurasādhvanivihitamudi, kadarthitakadambe kambudviṣi, prasṛtabisaprasūne, cakitacātake, viralavāride, tārataratārake, vāruṇīcārucandramasi, svādurasasalile, sphuritaśapharatarkubakoṭe, ghūkamaṇḍūkamaṇḍale, saṅkocitakañcukini, kāñcanacchedagauraśālini, krośadutkrośe, surabhigandhisaugandhikagandhahārihariṇāśve kumudāmodini kaumudīkṛtamudi, nibarhabarhiṇi, kūjatkoyaṣṭike, dhṛtadhārtarāṣṭre, hṛṣṭakalamagopikāgītasukhitamṛgayūthe, kathākṛtakiṃśuke, mlāpitamālatīlatāmukule, bandhūkabāndhave, sañjātakamuñjānake, visūtritasautrāmaṇadhanuṣi, smerakāśmīrarajaḥpiñjaritadiśi, vikasvarasare śaratsamayārambhe Kandarpaketuḥ paribhraman śilāmayīṃ putrikāṃ kautukena, mohena, śokena, vegena svapriyānukāriṇīti hastena pasparśa |
children.translated_text: Then, at the onset of the autumn season — when the wagtails (<s>khañjarīṭa</s>) were lively, the cranes (<s>krauñca</s>) freely roaming, the branches full of talkative <s>Bharadvāja</s> birds, the paddy fields bewildered with parrots mistaking [the grain for] vessels, the royal geese (rājahaṃsa) entering with passion, the horizon bright as the complexion of <s>Kaṃsāri</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), the royal rainclouds light as swan-down, the moon's great bow thickened, the sweet <s>madhu</s> (honey) grass flourishing, the ponds (<s>sāra</s>) resonant with the melodious calls of passionate <s>sārasa</s> cranes, the pools where piglets of sows greedy for <s>kaśeru</s> (water-chestnut) tubers dug up the banks now buzzing sweetly with flocks of <s>māṣaputrikā</s> insects, the <s>kadamba</s> trees scorned, the conch-shells silenced, the lotus (<s>bisa</s>) stalks spread out, the <s>cātaka</s> birds startled, the rain-clouds sparse, the stars twinkling brightly, the moon beautiful in <s>Vāruṇī</s>'s [quarter], the waters sweet-tasting, the <s>śaphara</s> fish and <s>baka</s> (crane) tips flashing, the circles of owls and frogs [retreating], the snakes contracted in their sheaths, the rice-fields golden as cut gold, the <s>krośa</s> birds crying, the <s>saugandhika</s> flower-fragrance stealing the deer, the <s>kumuda</s> (night-lily) fragrant, the moonlight making all joyful, the peacocks' tail-feathers shed, the <s>koyaṣṭika</s> (kingfisher) birds cooing, the <s>Dhārtarāṣṭra</s> geese arrived, the deer-herds gladdened by the singing of delighted rice-field maidens, the <s>kiṃśuka</s> (flame-of-the-forest) trees in tales, the jasmine vine-buds (<s>mālatī</s>) withered, the <s>bandhūka</s> flowers befriended, the <s>muñja</s> grass sprouted, the rainbow-bow of the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s> sacrifice unstrung, the directions tinged yellow with smiling saffron-dust, the lakes full and open — <s>Kandarpaketu</s>, while wandering, touched with his hand a stone figure, out of wonder, delusion, grief, and impulse, thinking it resembled his beloved.

children.text: anantaraṃ spṛṣṭamātrā sā śilāmayīṃ mūrtim utsṛjya, punar Vāsavadattā svarūpam āpede | tām avalokya Kandarpaketur amṛtārṇavamagna iva suciram āliṅgya papraccha | "priye kathaya kim idaṃ vṛttāntam" |
children.translated_text: Thereupon, the moment she was touched, she shed her stone form and once again <s>Vāsavadattā</s> attained her true nature. Beholding her, <s>Kandarpaketu</s>, as if immersed in an ocean of nectar, embraced her for a long time and asked: 'Beloved, tell me — what is this story?'

children.text: sā tu dīrgham uṣṇaṃ ca niḥśvasya kathayitum ārebhe | "āryaputrāpuṇyāyā mama mandabhāginyāḥ "kṛte mahābhāga ujjhitarājya" iti ekākī jana iva vāṅmanasayor agocaraṃ duḥkham anubhūtavān | anekadivasān āhāraśūnyatayā kṛśataro nidrānte yadi kadācit phalamūlādikaṃ milati, tadā śarīrasthitiṃ karotīti vicintya phalānveṣaṇāyopavanatarūn avalokayantī katipayanalvagocaram agaccham |
children.translated_text: <s>Vāsavadattā</s>, sighing long and hot, began to narrate: 'Noble lord, for the sake of this unlucky, ill-fated woman that I am, you, great one, having abandoned your kingdom, like a solitary person have endured suffering beyond the reach of speech and mind. For many days, growing thinner from lack of food, I thought: "If by chance after sleep he finds some fruits and roots, then he sustains his body." Thinking thus, searching for fruits, I went looking at the grove-trees and reached a place within a few <s>nalvas</s> (a unit of distance).'

children.text: krameṇa ca gulmāntaritakriyamāṇakāyamānikaṃ, viracyamāneśvaragṛhaṃ, avatāryamāṇakaṇṭhālakaṃ, ārabhyamāṇapaṭukaṭukaṃ, vyavasthāpyamānaveśyāsaṃniveśaṃ, śrūyamāṇaturagaheṣāravaṃ, vādyamānaviśrāmaḍhakkāpuṣkaraṃ, anviṣyamāṇasvādusalilāśayaṃ, uddiśyamānavipaṇiketuvāṃśaṃ senāsanniveśam apaśyam | tam avalokyāham acintayam | "kim ayaṃ mamānveṣaṇāya tātasya vyūha āhosvid āryaputrasya vāhinīsambhāra" iti cintayantyāṃ mayi paricārakakathitodanto mām uddiśya senāpatir dhāvitaḥ | tato 'nantaraṃ kirātasainyasenāpatis tādṛśa eva senāsamanvito mṛgayāvyājenāgataḥ so 'pi dāvitaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Gradually, I saw a military encampment — where measurements for tents were being taken hidden by thickets, where a lord's temple was being constructed, where neck-ornaments were being taken off, where sharp, pungent [food] was being prepared, where the quarters of courtesans were being arranged, where the neighing of horses was heard, where resting-drums and kettledrums were being sounded, where sweet water-reservoirs were being sought, where market-banner bamboo-poles were being erected. Seeing it, I wondered: "Is this my father's army deployed to search for me, or is it the noble lord's military force?" While I was thus thinking, a general, informed by an attendant about my identity, rushed towards me. Then immediately after, a <s>Kirāta</s> (tribal) army-chief, similarly accompanied by his troops, arrived under the pretext of a hunt — he too rushed [towards me].'

children.text: anantaraṃ cintitaṃ mayā | "yady aham āryaputrāya kathayāmi tadaikāky ebhir avaśyam eva hantavyaḥ | atha na kathayāmi tadāham evaibhir hantavyeti" cintākṣaṇa eva dvayoḥ sainyayor yuddham abhūd ekāmiṣābhiyuktayor gṛdhrayor iva | tataḥ pravṛttapratiśarāsāradurdinahṛtadinakarakiraṇe, rathakarmaviśāradadviradakaradūrotkṣiptakhaḍgadharasubhaṭaśliṣyamāṇavidyādharavibhrame, samaradarśanasañcaradanekanabhaścaracāraṇacakravāle, vetālasamākrāntaskandhakabandhacakrakriyamāṇacārupracāre, cārabhaṭakhaḍgakhaṇḍitadviradapādasamāptapiśācīkarṇolūkhalābharaṇakautuke, samutphullaphalakini, nadannāndīke, kāndiśīkabhīruṇi raṇakhale, sṛgālīprārthanīyeṣv āmiṣapiṇḍeṣv iva vatsadantakṣateṣu tṛṇeṣv iva, jihmagadaṣṭeṣv iva śarīreṣv anāsthāṃ kalayantaḥ samaṃ dviṣāṃ dhanuṣāṃ ca jīvākarṣaṇaṃ cakruḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Then I thought: "If I tell the noble lord, then, being alone, he will certainly be killed by them. But if I do not tell, then I myself will be killed by them." At that very moment of deliberation, the two armies began to fight — like two vultures competing for a single piece of flesh. Then, in a battlefield where the sunlight was stolen by the storm of arrows and counter-arrows, where warriors clutching swords hurled far by the trunks of elephants skilled in chariot-work embraced <s>Vidyādhara</s> (celestial being) illusions, where the horizon was filled with many sky-roaming <s>Cāraṇas</s> (celestial bards) coming to witness the battle, where <s>Vetāla</s> (vampiric spirits) mounted on the shoulders of headless trunks (<s>kabandha</s>) performed elegant maneuvers, where the amusement was created by ear-mortar ornaments of <s>piśācas</s> (demons) completed by the feet of elephants cut by the swords of <s>cārabhaṭa</s> (scout-warriors), where shields flashed, where battle-drums sounded, where cowards fled in all directions — in this battlefield, showing no more care for their bodies than for grass bruised by calves' teeth, or for bodies bitten by crooked [serpents], they simultaneously drew the life-strings of both their enemies and their bows.'

children.text: tyāgina iva dānavanto mārgaṇasantāpam asahantaḥ mahāmṛgā utkupitā iva kṣamāṃ muñcantas turagā rejuḥ | karṇābhyāṃ paraparivādaśravaṇakutūhalibhyāṃ, netrābhyām ālokitasādhuvipattibhyāṃ, mūrdhnā cāsthāne praṇamatā "tyakto 'ham" iti harṣād eva nanarta ciraṃ kabandhaḥ |
children.translated_text: Like generous donors (<s>dānavantaḥ</s>, pun: demons) unable to bear the pain of arrows (<s>mārgaṇa</s>, pun: seeking/begging), the great beasts (elephants) shone; like the angry earth (<s>kṣamā</s>, pun: patience) releasing [itself], the horses blazed. With ears eager to hear slander against others, with eyes that had witnessed the misfortune of the virtuous, and with his head bowing in the wrong place — a headless trunk (<s>kabandha</s>) danced for a long time in sheer joy, [crying] 'I am free!'

children.text:
tataḥ parihāseneva cakṣuṣī pidadhatā parāpavādaśravaṇāruṇeva śrotravṛttiṃ sthagayatā, sonmādeneva vāyuvegavikṣiptena, palitaṅkaraṇeneva surayoṣitāṃ, andhaṃkaraṇeneva yodhānāṃ, timireṇeva samarapradoṣasya, patiteneva vimuktagotreṇa, mīmāṃsakadarśaneneva tiraskṛtadigambaradarśanena, satpuruṣeṇeva viṣṇupadāvalambinā samarajena rajasā jajṛmbhe |
tatra samarasambhāre kaścid āśaṅkitorubhaṅgaḥ suyodhana iva yodhaḥ payasi viveśa | kaścic charatalpaśayo bhīṣma iva cirāya śvasann āsīt | kaścit karṇa iva viklavībhūtasarvāṅgaḥ śaktimokṣaṇam akarot | tato vidhvastadhvajapaṭaṃ patatpatākaṃ cyutacāpacāmarāpīḍaṃ skhalatkhaḍgadhenukaṃ tatsamastasainyam anyonyaṃ nidhanam avāpa |
children.translated_text: Then the dust of battle spread mightily — as if in mockery, covering the eyes; like redness from hearing others' slander, blocking the function of hearing; as if with frenzy, hurled by the force of the wind; causing graying like [it does] to divine women; causing blindness like [it does] to warriors; like the darkness of battle's nightfall; like a fallen one whose lineage is abandoned; like the <s>Mīmāṃsaka</s> philosophical view, obscuring the Digambara (Jain) view; like a virtuous man, clinging to the feet of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. In that carnage of battle, one warrior, fearing his thigh was broken, entered the water like <s>Suyodhana</s> (<s>Duryodhana</s>). Another, lying on a bed of arrows, like <s>Bhīṣma</s>, lay breathing for a long time. Another, with all limbs enfeebled, like <s>Karṇa</s>, discharged his lance. Then that entire army, on both sides, with their banner-cloths destroyed, their flags falling, their bows, whisks, and diadems dropped, their sword-hilts slipping — met mutual destruction.

children.text: anantaraṃ yasyāśramas tena muninā puṣpādikam ādāyāgatena pratipannasarvavṛttāntena "mamāyam āśramo bhagna iti śilāmayī bhaveti" śaptāham | anantaraṃ "varākī bahuduḥkham anubhavatīti" karuṇayāryaputrasya sparśāvadhi śāpāntam akarot |"
children.translated_text: "Thereafter, by that sage — whose hermitage it was — who had returned bringing flowers and the like and who had learned all the events, I was cursed: 'Since my hermitage has been destroyed, may you become stone.' Then, [thinking] 'the poor woman is enduring much suffering,' out of compassion he set the end of the curse at the touch of the noble lord."

children.text: tataḥ Kandarpaketuḥ samāgatena Makarandena Vāsavadattayā saha svapuraṃ gatvā hṛdayābhilaṣitāni tāni tāni suratasukhāny anubhavan kālaṃ nināya ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Kandarpaketu</s>, reunited with <s>Makaranda</s>, went with <s>Vāsavadattā</s> to his own city, and passed the time experiencing those various heart-desired pleasures of love.

body.text: iti mahākavi-Subandhu-viracitā Vāsavadattā nāma kathā samāptā |
body.translated_text: Thus ends the story named <s>Vāsavadattā</s>, composed by the great poet <s>Subandhu</s>.
